Job Description:

Overview

The Program Analyst/Procurement Analyst supports the RADS project by coordinating procurement workflows, managing purchasing documentation, and ensuring financial alignment across systems such as SC360, Jira, Confluence, and SharePoint. This office-based role performs work directly related to management and general business operations, exercising discretion and independent judgment in shaping processes, interpreting contract requirements, and making binding decisions within delegated authority.

The analyst refines procurement and administrative procedures, resolves process issues, and collaborates with cross-functional teams and vendors to influence key business decisions and maintain compliance. The role supports program leadership with operational and administrative tasks, demonstrating authority to adapt workflows and negotiate outcomes of significance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, implement, and refine procurement and administrative processes to optimize program operations and ensure compliance with organizational policies.
  • Assess and interpret contract requirements, federal regulations, and organizational policies to guide purchasing actions and resolve ambiguities.
  • Provide expert advice to program leadership on procurement strategy, risk mitigation, and process improvements, influencing key business decisions.
  • Shape and adapt procurement workflows and documentation standards, independently determining effective methods for tracking, reporting, and compliance.
  • Process procurement actions in SC360, ensuring accurate financial coding, data flow, and compliance with GDIT workflows.
  • Initiate, track, and manage procurement requests, including Asset Intake Requests (AIRs), Bills of Materials (BOMs), Purchase Requisitions (PRs), and Purchase Orders (POs).
  • Apply an understanding of the complete software asset lifecycle to support software acquisition, deployment, usage tracking, renewals, and disposition.
  • Coordinate cross-functional projects involving finance, procurement, and program management to support organizational objectives and business operations.
  • Collaborate with technical SMEs, program managers, internal procurement staff, and federal stakeholders to ensure purchases align with contract scope, program needs, and delivery timelines.
  • Collaborate with vendors and service providers, making binding decisions within delegated authority to ensure optimal program outcomes.
  • Maintain communication among vendors, internal procurement teams, program staff, and federal partners to ensure smooth contract execution.
  • Organize and maintain procurement documentation—including product pages, vendor contacts, usage reports, support details, and renewal tracking—across Confluence, SharePoint, and internal trackers.
  • Update and maintain Confluence documentation related to procurement workflows, staff training requirements, contractual reports, status reports, operational updates, and software licensing information.
  • Provide administrative support to RADS leadership, including meeting logistics, contractual reporting tasks, and communication coordination.
  • Support onboarding activities by preparing documentation, coordinating tasks with leadership, and assisting with SOP updates, process improvements, and workflow optimization.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree
  • 2+ years of experience in procurement, purchasing workflows, finance support, or contract administration.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of enterprise purchasing and requisition systems such as SC360, SAP Ariba, Coupa, Oracle iProcurement, or similar.
  • Experience with Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and SharePoint.
  • Experience managing and tracking different types of software licenses (e.g., subscription, perpetual, enterprise).
  • Attention to detail with accurate data entry, documentation, and tracking abilities.
  • Strong organizational and time-management skills; ability to manage multiple concurrent actions.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook).
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience supporting GDIT programs or large federal government contractors in SC360 or a similar system.
  • Familiarity with federal procurement workflows, compliance requirements, and government contract financial management.
  • Experience with inventory management, software asset tracking, or license administration.
  • Exposure to Agile environments or Scrum workflows.

As cybersecurity incidents exceed the capabilities and scope of Tier 2 operations, the Tier 3 Incident Commander serves as the senior operational lead responsible for coordinating advanced incident response, driving resolution, and ensuring effective communication across stakeholders. The Tier 3 Incident Commander leads a 24x7x365 incident coordination function, responding to escalated alerts, notifications, and incident reports. Responsibilities include establishing and maintaining incident situational awareness, tracking incident progression, coordinating response and remediation activities, facilitating recovery efforts, communicating with stakeholders, and delivering timely, accurate incident reporting.

The role requires the ability to assess complex cybersecurity events, analyze adversary motives, capabilities, and opportunities, and determine the potential impact, scope, and severity of an incident. The Incident Commander ensures that incident reports are accurately documented in the incident tracking system, coordinates with reporting entities to validate information and establish a comprehensive understanding of the event, and identifies additional investigative, containment, remediation, or recovery actions required to achieve resolution.

The Tier 3 Incident Commander must possess extensive knowledge of cybersecurity incident response, anomaly detection and analysis, security log analysis, digital forensics, threat vectors, and adversary tactics and techniques. The individual must be able to interpret technical findings, assess incident reports, exercise sound judgment, and direct or coordinate appropriate response activities based on established procedures and incident requirements. The role also requires strict adherence to standard operating procedures (SOPs), organizational policies, and established escalation, notification, and reporting protocols, including the timely notification and communication of incidents to Federal leadership.

Required technical expertise includes a strong working knowledge of Splunk Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Microsoft Defender Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Palo Alto Networks Cortex XSOAR, and supporting digital forensic and incident response tools.

Required Experience:

  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant professional experience, or a bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years of relevant experience.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen and able to complete a federal background investigation for a High-Risk Public Trust position, including applicable credit checks.
  • Must hold CISSP certification from ISC2, plus GCIH (GIAC Certified Incident Handler) or an equivalent relevant incident response, digital forensics, or cybersecurity certification.
  • Extensive experience managing cybersecurity incidents, performing advanced incident triage, coordinating response activities, and driving investigations through resolution.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Security Operations Center (SOC) operations, threat hunting, intrusion detection and prevention, security event monitoring, and incident detection and response.
  • Expert knowledge of TCP/IP protocols, network traffic analysis, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), and security log analysis, including the ability to distinguish genuine threats from false positives.
  • Experience with endpoint security, antivirus, endpoint detection and response (EDR), host-based intrusion detection, firewalls, proxies, web application firewalls (WAF), and other enterprise security solutions, including FireEye products.
  • Extensive experience analyzing and correlating security logs from diverse systems and security devices, identifying suspicious activity, and collecting relevant host, network, and cloud data to support investigations.
  • Strong understanding of Windows and Unix/Linux operating systems, enterprise networking, system and application security, systems and network administration, and operating system hardening.
  • Knowledge of digital forensic techniques, including evidence collection, recovery, preservation, chain of custody, and acquisition of forensic images, logs, and other artifacts to support investigations and remediation.
  • Understanding of cyberattack stages, adversary techniques, threat profiling, host-based and network-based intrusion detection, and methods for identifying indicators of compromise.
  • Experience creating and tracking incident investigations, preparing security alert notifications, maintaining accurate incident records, and documenting response activities through resolution.
  • Experience supporting or advising on compliance with security frameworks and regulatory requirements, including FISMA, PCI DSS, GDPR, NIST, and ISO standards.
  • Understanding of Computer Network Defense (CND) policies, procedures, standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Ability to coordinate incident response teams, work with senior business leaders to understand business objectives, assess risks, and communicate effective mitigation strategies.
  • Ability to clearly communicate complex cybersecurity findings, incident details, and recommended actions to technical teams, incident responders, senior executives, and non-technical stakeholders, including during crises.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, presentation, facilitation, documentation, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple investigations and competing priorities simultaneously.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct advanced incident response analysis to identify attack vectors, assess threats, and investigate malware, data exposure, phishing, social engineering, and other cybersecurity incidents.
  • Coordinate incident containment, remediation, and recovery activities to mitigate threats and restore affected systems and services.
  • Monitor and analyze security events and alerts from Splunk SIEM and other security tools; review escalated alerts and perform Level 3 incident triage to determine incident type, severity, scope, risk, and appropriate response or escalation.
  • Serve as the primary point of coordination for incident management, assigning response actions and coordinating stakeholders, enterprise teams, resources, and timelines during significant incidents, including data breaches and ransomware attacks.
  • Create, maintain, and track incident records and ticket queues from initial detection through investigation, remediation, resolution, and closure, ensuring accurate documentation and compliance with federal requirements, departmental policies, and applicable legislation.
  • Evaluate and recommend technical, procedural, and physical security controls to address vulnerabilities, mitigate incident impact, reduce risk, and prevent recurrence.
  • Prepare incident status reports, executive briefings, and post-incident reports documenting findings, response actions, remediation, recovery, lessons learned, and restoration of normal operations.
  • Collaborate with digital forensic investigators and application security analysts on incident investigations and threat-hunting activities, conducting or coordinating endpoint, network, and log analysis to identify indicators of compromise, determine incident scope, and support root-cause analysis.

Position Overview

The Senior Channel Marketing Manager will lead Volcora’s channel, brand, content, digital, and industry marketing programs.

This person will be responsible for turning Volcora’s business priorities into structured marketing campaigns that increase brand awareness, support channel partners, generate qualified opportunities, and strengthen Volcora’s position within the POS, payments, retail technology, and hospitality technology industries.

This is a hands-on role. The Senior Channel Marketing Manager will set strategy, but must also be comfortable writing campaign messaging, reviewing content, building presentations, coordinating events, launching emails, managing partners, and analyzing campaign performance.

The ideal candidate has experience marketing B2B technology, hardware, SaaS, payments, or other products sold through partners, resellers, distributors, or strategic alliances.

Key Responsibilities

Marketing Strategy and Planning

  • Develop and execute Volcora’s annual marketing plan in alignment with revenue, channel, product, and business-development goals.

  • Establish clear messaging, target audiences, campaign priorities, content themes, and performance objectives.

  • Translate company objectives into quarterly and monthly marketing programs.

  • Manage the marketing calendar, budget, resources, agencies, freelancers, and campaign timelines.

  • Identify the marketing activities that will have the greatest impact on partner engagement, qualified pipeline, and industry visibility.

  • Regularly evaluate campaign performance and adjust priorities based on results.

Channel and Partner Marketing

  • Develop and manage marketing programs for Volcora’s resellers, ISVs, payment partners, processors, distributors, and strategic partners.

  • Strengthen and promote Volcora’s partner program through communications, onboarding, enablement, and co-marketing.

  • Create monthly partner campaign packages that may include emails, social content, landing pages, product materials, and lead-generation offers.

  • Develop co-branded campaigns, webinars, case studies, partner spotlights, and event programs.

  • Create partner toolkits containing product images, sales presentations, social templates, email copy, competitive materials, and other resources.

  • Work with sales to identify priority partners and develop account-specific marketing plans.

  • Increase partner participation in campaigns, product launches, webinars, events, and customer-development initiatives.

  • Establish processes for tracking partner engagement, partner-sourced opportunities, and marketing-influenced revenue.

Brand Positioning and Messaging

  • Strengthen and consistently communicate Volcora’s position as a channel-focused provider of reliable and deployment-ready POS hardware.

  • Develop clear messaging for different audiences, including VARs, ISVs, processors, distributors, and multi-location operators.

  • Maintain brand voice, visual standards, product messaging, and company positioning across all channels.

  • Ensure product specifications are translated into meaningful business benefits.

  • Review and approve major marketing communications before publication.

  • Help organize Volcora’s growing product portfolio into understandable solution categories and market narratives.

  • Monitor competitor positioning and identify opportunities for Volcora to differentiate.

Demand Generation and Campaign Management

  • Plan and execute integrated campaigns across email, social media, website, events, webinars, partner channels, and targeted advertising.

  • Create campaigns supporting product launches, partner recruitment, hardware upgrades, vertical solutions, and industry events.

  • Build audience segments and lead-nurturing campaigns for partners, prospects, and existing customers.

  • Collaborate with sales to define campaign follow-up processes and lead qualification standards.

  • Develop campaign landing pages, offers, calls to action, and conversion paths.

  • Track leads from initial engagement through qualified opportunity and revenue where possible.

  • Test messaging, formats, audiences, and campaign channels to improve performance.

Email Marketing and Marketing Automation

  • Own Volcora’s email marketing strategy, including newsletters, product announcements, partner communications, event campaigns, and nurture programs.

  • Develop segmentation based on partner type, account status, product interest, purchasing history, engagement, and industry.

  • Build automated communications for partner onboarding, customer nurturing, event follow-up, and product education.

  • Ensure contact lists are organized, accurate, compliant, and appropriately segmented.

  • Review email performance and improve open rates, click rates, responses, conversions, and deliverability.

  • Coordinate closely with sales so email campaigns support active account-development priorities.

Content and Thought Leadership

  • Develop Volcora’s editorial strategy across articles, case studies, technical guides, social media, email, webinars, and video.

  • Identify topics that build authority in POS hardware, retail technology, payments, deployment, device lifecycle, kiosks, KDS, and unattended retail.

  • Interview partners, customers, executives, sales representatives, and technical personnel.

  • Produce or oversee case studies, partner stories, white papers, product guides, blog articles, and industry commentary.

  • Turn technical information into clear, credible, and commercially useful content.

  • Repurpose core content across email, LinkedIn, sales materials, webinars, videos, and partner campaigns.

  • Develop a consistent schedule of educational and promotional content.

  • Ensure content is accurate, useful, differentiated, and aligned with Volcora’s brand.

Social Media and Community Leadership

  • Own Volcora’s social media strategy, with LinkedIn as the primary B2B platform.

  • Guide the Marketing & Community Specialist in maintaining the content calendar and daily community engagement.

  • Develop recurring content series covering partner stories, deployments, products, technical education, events, and company updates.

  • Increase engagement from relevant industry professionals rather than focusing only on general follower growth.

  • Establish an employee advocacy program that helps sales, product, support, and leadership share relevant content.

  • Monitor industry conversations, partner activity, competitor communications, and emerging topics.

  • Build meaningful relationships with channel professionals, partners, customers, associations, and industry communities.

Events, Trade Shows, and Webinars

  • Develop marketing strategies for RetailNOW, NRF, regional payments events, partner conferences, webinars, and other industry programs.

  • Treat each event as an integrated campaign spanning pre-event promotion, scheduled meetings, on-site content, and post-event follow-up.

  • Develop event themes, booth messaging, presentations, invitations, landing pages, social campaigns, and follow-up communications.

  • Coordinate partner dinners, roundtables, webinars, product demonstrations, and other engagement programs.

  • Ensure leads are captured, organized, assigned, followed up, and measured.

  • Evaluate events based on qualified meetings, pipeline, partner engagement, and eventual revenue—not only booth traffic.

Product Marketing and Sales Enablement

  • Develop positioning, messaging, and go-to-market plans for new and existing products.

  • Produce sales presentations, competitive battlecards, solution briefs, product-selection guides, compatibility materials, and FAQs.

  • Gather feedback from partners, customers, and sales teams to improve product messaging and market fit.

  • Coordinate marketing support for emerging product lines such as kiosks, KDS, mobile devices, vending, and IoT solutions.

Website and Digital Presence

  • Develop pages for specific audiences, solutions, industries, products, campaigns, and partner programs.

  • Coordinate with designers, developers, SEO resources, and internal stakeholders.

  • Review website analytics and identify opportunities to increase qualified traffic and conversions.

About the Role:

The Data Science team is expanding and is looking for a Data Scientist to help build the next generation of agentic systems for cybersecurity. CrowdStrike's cybersecurity data is one-of-a-kind: we process nearly a trillion behavioral events per day. You'll work where Machine Learning, Big Data, and Cybersecurity converge — training models, building AI agents, and rigorously measuring whether they work — on data and problems you won't find anywhere else.

  • Research new approaches to agentic planning, and prototype state-of-the-art methods from the literature

  • Optimize prompts and inference to get the most out of every model
  • Collaborate and coordinate across Engineering, Data Science, and Managed Services teams, and partner with engineers to take prototypes toward production
  • Keep track of developments in the field of Artificial Intelligence and help identify, define, and prioritize areas for research

  • PhD-level depth of understanding in modern machine learning research —a doctorate itself is not required, but we expect equivalent mastery, including the ability to read, critique, implement, and improve upon current papers
  • Experience training generative models, with a strong command of LLM training fundamentals (architecture, optimization, tokenization, data, and scaling behavior)
  • Reinforcement learning / post-training as a core skill: RLHF/RLAIF, policy optimization (PPO/GRPO/DPO), reward modeling, and building RL environments for agents
  • Experience building agentic systems: agent architectures (ReAct, planning, reflection), tool and function calling, and retrieval/memory/context management
  • Experience with systematic prompt optimization, and with designing and building evals for LLM systems
  • Fluency with GPUs, PyTorch, and the common LLM training and serving stack (e.g., Hugging Face Transformers/TRL/PEFT, DeepSpeed/FSDP, vLLM/TGI/SGLang)
  • Strong, reproducible research engineering: clean Python and disciplined experiment tracking that your collaborators can build on
  • Ability to work independently on ambiguous and complex objectives, and to communicate clearly within a large project team
  • Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience generating training data and environments — synthetic data, agent trajectories/rollouts, and task simulators
  • Familiarity with inference-time scaling / test-time compute (search, self-consistency, verifier-guided decoding, long chain-of-thought)
  • Experience with agent safety and guardrails: sandboxing, abuse/jailbreak resistance, and reliability for autonomous systems
  • A knack for interpretability and failure analysis — diagnosing why a model or agent fails, not just that it does
  • Notable open-source contributions and excellent technical writing
  • Passionate about cybersecurity, with a firm understanding of the problem space — or passionate about applying your machine-learning skillset to a new domain such as cybersecurity (a security background is a plus, not a requirement)

Overview

Nakupuna Companies is looking for a Database Administrator to provide Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Business Systems Center (BSC) contractor support services for the team. Support services include database design and development, performance tuning, testing, backup and recovery, release support, documentation, and coordination with application-development teams.

Responsibilities

The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign additional duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons.

  • Design and implement databases to meet application requirements.

  • Optimize database performance through indexing, caching, and query optimization.

  • Develop and execute database test plans, including unit, integration, and performance testing.
  • Collaborate with application developers to ensure database designs meet application requirements.
  • Develop and implement backup and recovery plans that protect data integrity and availability.
  • Manage database instances, including their creation, configuration, and deletion.
  • Use the enterprise-wide version-control system and support secure, quality-controlled CI/CD builds, testing, and deployments.
  • Identify, define, or modify interfaces with other systems and applications, ensuring agreements are formally documented with the interfacing system or application.
  • Support production outages, development of release packages, work-item updates in the designated tool, and internal review or change boards.
  • Conduct quality audits of NAVSUP products, perform causative research on errors, and provide corrective action.
  • Maintain a professional relationship with clients, team members, and internal and external agencies and organizations.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications: Shall have two years or more of experience and knowledge in the following areas:

  • Two or more years of experience and knowledge performing database administration, data management, database engineering, or related software-engineering activities.
  • Knowledge of the design and implementation of computer and database-management systems.
  • Knowledge of current software and database engineering methodologies, design techniques, and applicable software and database standards.
  • Experience using Structured Query Language (SQL) and Microsoft SQL Server database-development capabilities.

  • Experience with service-based architectures, APIs, REST, SOAP, or event-driven architectures.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree with a technical major, such as engineering, computer science, information systems, or a related discipline, is required. The degree requirement may be substituted with two years of college or technical education and three to five years of related work experience.

Experience with government and DoD environments is desired.

jobs.excerpt: Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners.
jobs.description:
Flex is building the AI-native private bank for business owners.
We’re re-architecting the entire financial system for entrepreneurs—from the first dollar a business earns to how that value compounds, moves, and is ultimately spent in real life. Banking, credit, payments, personal finance, and financial operations—rebuilt from the ground up as a single, intelligent system. Flex is the full financial home for ambitious owners.
Since launching publicly in September 2023, Flex has scaled from zero to nine-figure annualized revenue, with a clear path to profitability by late 2026. We move fast, ship relentlessly, and operate with extreme ownership.
Our customers are affluent business owners ($3–$200M in revenue)—the backbone of the economy and one of the most underserved segments in finance. They’re stuck with outdated banks and fragmented tools. We’re replacing all of it. The opportunity is massive: a ~$1T+ revenue market hiding in plain sight. Our ambition is to build a $100B+ company by delivering a product that is fundamentally better—not incrementally improved.
Flex has raised $100M+ in equity and $300M+ in debt.
- Mission-critical problems: We build software that directly controls how money moves at scale.
- High bar, low ego: Small teams, exceptional people, real ownership.
- Speed over comfort: We prioritize execution, quality, clarity, and results.
- Enduring impact: What we’re building will define how a generation of owners runs their businesses.

Team & Locations

We hire exceptional people who want to build hard things and see their work matter immediately. Roles are available in: San Francisco, Miami, New York, and fully remote.

Flex Fuels Ambition.

About The Role

    Flex is hiring a General Manager to build and run its venture and private equity business. You own the sector end to end: the strategy for winning it, the relationships and partnerships that open it, the product priorities it needs, and the P&L it produces. You build on Flex’s platform, balance sheet and teams, and you are responsible for making Flex the primary financial institution for venture and private equity.

    The role is modeled on sector coverage at an investment bank. You decide which relationships matter, which partnerships can move hundreds of owners onto Flex at once, and what the product must deliver to win them. Flex’s product, credit, risk and member experience teams execute and service alongside you. The role reports directly to the CEO.

    Funds are the most efficient path to hundreds of owners at once. A sponsor that standardizes its portfolio on Flex, or a venture firm whose founders bank with Flex from their first wire, delivers in one decision what would otherwise take a hundred. The decision sits with general partners, fund CFOs, operating partners, fund administrators and fund-finance lenders. The General Manager owns those relationships.

What You'll Do

    • 7 to 12 years in investment banking, private credit, private equity, venture, or a senior commercial seat inside venture and private equity. You have a demonstrable record of originating business, not servicing it.

    • An active network in venture and private equity. You can name the 50 people who matter and most of them would take your call this week.

    • Fluent in how funds and their portfolio companies move money: capital calls and distributions, portfolio treasury and credit, operating-partner priorities, and what a portfolio CFO requires to move a banking relationship.

    • Comfortable structuring partnerships, negotiating referral economics, and working through a term sheet without support.

    • You build your own models. Banker-level Excel and a working understanding of the unit economics of deposits, cards and credit.

Requirements

    • 7 to 12 years in investment banking, private credit, private equity, venture, or a senior commercial seat inside construction. You have a demonstrable record of originating business, not servicing it.

    • An active network in construction. You can name the 50 people who matter and most of them would take your call this week.

    • Fluent in how contractors are paid and where their capital gets tied up: margins, working capital, pay applications, retainage, bonding, and who lends against each.

    • Comfortable structuring partnerships, negotiating referral economics, and working through a term sheet without support.

    • You build your own models. Banker-level Excel and a working understanding of the unit economics of deposits, cards and credit.

Nice To Haves

    • Experience in fintech, banking or lending, or selling a financial product to business owners.

    • A standing in venture and private equity: a podcast, a newsletter, a conference stage, or a board seat at a trade body.

    • Investing, advisory or operating experience in a company in venture and private equity.

How To Prepare

    As part of the application, please be prepared to submit a one-pager along with your CV on how you would bring venture and private equity to Flex. It should cover:

    • The sector and its owners. Who they are, how many of them fall in Flex’s range, how they make money and where their capital gets tied up.

    • What they need from a bank. The products and terms that would make owners in the sector move their primary relationship, and in what order.

    • The map. The 20 to 30 people and institutions that move the sector, and how many of them you know personally.

    • The first three partnerships. The programs that would put hundreds of owners on Flex at once, and why each counterparty would say yes.

    • The investment and the return. A light P&L for the sector: what Flex would need to put in over the first two years (people, product, partnership economics, marketing) and how that investment comes back, in the form of owners banking with Flex and the revenue they produce. We are looking for the shape of the business and the logic behind it.

    • The plan and the team. How you will build this out and what you will need to do it.

      • Treat it as a coverage pitch. Bring the map, the partnerships and the economics, and be ready to defend each one.

Why Join Us

Build something generational — Capture the full lifecycle of money for ambitious business owners.
Work on real money, real risk — Payments, credit, and banking at serious scale.
Solve hard problems — AI, underwriting, compliance, and global finance from first principles.
True ownership — Small teams, high trust, real accountability.
Founder-level exposure — Direct access to leadership, customers, and investors.
High bar, high taste — Move fast without cutting corners.
Elite peers — People here are builders, not tourists.
Real upside — Meaningful equity if you help build something big.

jobs.description:
ABOUT STORD


Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.


By combining comprehensive commerce-enablement technology with high-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator-built software suite including OMS, Pre- and Post-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.


With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end-to-end commerce solutions combine best-in-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.


Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like True Classic, Native, Seed Health, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.

Stord is hiring a remote Lead Brand Designer to own and evolve its visual identity across the website, product marketing, events, sales collateral, and social. It's a hands-on player-coach role. You'll set creative direction, build scalable brand guidelines and templates, guide a small team of designers and freelancers, and still design high-impact work yourself. You'll partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Gen, Content, Sales, Product Design, and leadership. We're looking for 8+ years of brand design experience (2+ leading), advanced Figma and Adobe skills, a strong portfolio, and someone organized and comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-paced environment.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Are you a seasoned Swiss Army knife brand designer with the appetite to both lead and execute world-class designs, ranging from website redesigns and experiential activations to OOH, print, and more, with equal parts speed and precision? If so, read on! We're on the hunt for a Lead Brand Designer who can help us bring the brand to life and ensure the world knows Stord as the leader in commerce.


In this role, you will focus on defining, evolving, and protecting Stord's visual identity across every place customers, brands, and prospects meet us, from the website and product marketing to events, sales collateral, and social. You will translate Stord's positioning as The Consumer Experience Company into a distinctive, cohesive brand system that builds trust, sharpens differentiation, and supports pipeline growth and brand awareness. This role is a hands-on player-coach: a creative leader with strong craft who sets the design direction, raises the bar for the team's work, and still opens the files and ships.

You will have the opportunity to guide a small team of designers and freelance partners, and you will partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Content, Sales, Product Design, and Executive leadership. Expect a fast-moving, collaborative environment where brand decisions connect directly to business outcomes. This is a remote opportunity.


What You'll Do

  • Own the brand system: Maintain and evolve Stord's visual identity, including logo, color, typography, illustration, iconography, photography, motion, and layout, and keep it documented in clear, usable guidelines and templates.
  • Set creative direction: Define the design vision for campaigns, launches, the website, events, and sales enablement, and ensure every asset looks and feels unmistakably Stord.
  • Design high-impact work: Create standout assets across digital and print, such as landing pages, ads, decks, one-pagers, social content, trade show environments, and swag, from concept through final production.
  • Lead and coach the team: Guide designers and freelancers, give clear and constructive feedback, set quality standards, manage priorities and workflow, and help team members grow their craft.
  • Partner across the business: Work with Product Marketing, Demand Gen, Content, Sales, and Product Design to turn briefs and business goals into compelling creative, and balance speed with quality as priorities shift.
  • Scale brand consistency: Build reusable templates, design components, and self-serve resources so teams across Stord can produce on-brand work quickly, and review high-visibility work for brand alignment.
  • Connect design to results: Use performance data, feedback, and testing to inform creative decisions, and show how brand work contributes to awareness, engagement, and pipeline.
  • Manage agencies and vendors: Brief, direct, and review work from external creative partners, printers, and production vendors, and manage creative budgets where applicable.

What You'll Need

  • Bachelor's degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Fine Arts, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 7+ years of brand or graphic design experience, including 2+ years leading projects, designers, or creative direction. B2B technology, SaaS, or supply chain and logistics experience is a plus.
  • Brand systems expertise: A track record of building or evolving a brand identity and scalable guidelines that teams actually use.
  • Visual craft: Exceptional typography, layout, color, and composition skills across digital, print, and presentation formats, backed by a strong portfolio.
  • Design tools fluency: Advanced proficiency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite (Illustrator, Photoshop, InDesign), plus experience with Google Slides or PowerPoint for sales and executive decks.
  • Leadership and feedback: Proven ability to coach designers, give actionable critique, and manage creative workflow, intake, and deadlines.
  • Cross-functional communication: Ability to present and defend design decisions to stakeholders, translate business goals into creative, and collaborate with Marketing, Sales, and Product.
  • Project management: Exceptional organization and the ability to develop systems that allow both the team and yourself to do your best work.
  • Fast-paced adaptability: Experience and comfort working in a fast-paced environment with ambiguity.

Bonus Points

  • Motion design and video skills (After Effects, Premiere, or similar), and familiarity with Webflow, HubSpot, or other web and marketing platforms.
  • Experience using AI-assisted design tools responsibly to speed up concepting and production while protecting brand quality.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Graphic Design or Visual Communication from a program with a strong branding focus.
  • Experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS, e-commerce, logistics, or supply chain technology company, or at a brand-focused design agency.

We are a female-founded scale-up, currently made up of around 100 AltoVitians. Our fully-remote team hails from 26 different countries and collectively speaks 29 languages. Being humble is important because it enables us to keep learning every day, and tenacity is necessary because in a high performing environment as fast-paced as AltoVita, taking it slow is simply not an option!

As we look to scale our Global Commercial engine, today is a particularly exciting time to join our team. This next chapter won’t always be a smooth ride, but it will be filled with innovation, excitement and opportunities. If you are ambitious, commercially hungry and ready for the challenge (and the fun!) of growing with us, we would love to hear from you.

What we do

AltoVita is a multi-award winning accommodation platform that enables enterprises to consolidate accommodation programmes through the power of proprietary technology paired with a human centric approach.

AltoVita’s unique offering sets us apart in the market, providing a network of 10 million+ verified and vetted properties are all duty of care compliant, backed by a four-tier quality control process; located in over 35,000 cities & 165 countries world-wide. With our award-winning enterprise software and human-centric approach, we deliver smart and sustainable solutions to global talent mobility & business travel managers worldwide.

Our Client Development team plays a vital role as trusted advisors and partners to our clients. Embodying our consultative philosophy, this dedicated team proactively shares new market insights, analyzes data, and empowers our clients with the tools and knowledge to make informed decisions, ensuring our clients are always equipped to make the best choices for their corporate housing needs.

AltoVita’s technology provides a cloud-based bridge between the highly fragmented property distribution system and multinational Global 2000 companies. A proprietary two-way API integration with a standardized sourcing process reduces the legacy, inefficient 48-to-72-hour bidding process down to a few minutes, saving valuable time and money.

Corporate clients love the bespoke user interface seamlessly configured to their mobility policies, and employees enjoy a greater sense of choice and support in their relocation journey.

About the role

The Director of Sales, US, will support AltoVita's Sales and Business Development efforts in the region, reporting into the SVP Sales, US. This is an external facing role focused on building credible relationships, opening doors with new prospects, and creating qualified opportunities.

This is a mid-level opportunity for someone ambitious, commercially hungry, and highly coachable, with real potential to grow into a more senior sales role at AltoVita as you prove yourself.

  • Identify new business opportunities within the US, including new markets, growth areas, trends, customers, and services.

  • Consistently elevate AltoVita’s brand awareness through thought leadership, LinkedIn presence, and hosting high-impact webinars, roundtables and industry events.

  • Work with the Marketing team to support lead acquisition and nurturing.

  • Leverage your network to build genuine, credible relationships with prospective clients, employees, and other stakeholders, bringing a client centric, “above and beyond” mindset to how you serve them.

  • Meet with prospects face to face or virtually, and attend relevant conferences and industry events to build AltoVita's presence in the market, planning travel efficiently to maximize ROI.

  • Act as a trusted first point of contact, earning credibility and open doors that convert into qualified sales opportunities.

  • Keep abreast of trends and changes in relocation, business travel, hospitality, corporate housing, and serviced apartment industries.

  • Develop, forecast, and report on your sales funnel whilst demonstrating full accountability, keeping CRM and documentation accurate and up to date.

  • Optimize travel between the region to maximize sales efforts and minimize expenses.

  • Clearly and consistently communicate pipeline progress to your line managers and internal stakeholders.

  • Collaborate with the Product and Client Development teams to feed back client needs and market learnings.

  • Hand off qualified opportunities to the enablement/closing team at the right stage, ensuring a smooth transition and a clear client handover.

  • Learn and upscale to new verticals and geographies that are important for the company.

What you will bring:

  • Core: strategic thinking, innovation, sound decision making, strong collaboration & communication, comfort with change, agility, and a client-centric mindset.
  • Leadership: ownership & accountability, resource and performance management, and a track record of developing others (as your book of business and any team grow).
  • Meta: a strong learning orientation, critical thinking & problem solving, and adaptability & resilience.

Who you are:

  • 3+ years experience within the business travel or corporate housing industry

  • Tenacious and driven

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, sometimes less structured and entrepreneurial environment

  • Able to think strategically

Ways of Working

AltoVita is a fully remote team. Although we have regular touch-points throughout the week, organize off-sites in several locations, trust is essential for us to work effectively as a team. Join our Team

jobs.excerpt: Job Summary The Senior Analyst, OON Dispute Analytics and Reporting, supports the out-of-network (OON) provider liability operating model by developing the analytics, reporting, and market intelligence needed to inform the negotiation strategy, arbitration positioning, QPA payment accuracy, and overall IDR performance.
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Senior Analyst, OON Dispute Analytics and Reporting, supports the out-of-network (OON) provider liability operating model by developing the analytics, reporting, and market intelligence needed to inform the negotiation strategy, arbitration positioning, QPA payment accuracy, and overall IDR performance. The role reports to the Director, Provider Dispute Strategy, and serves as the primary analytics partner for pre-IDR negotiation, federal NSA IDR, state-based dispute processes, and provider-level OON liability management. The Senior Analyst is responsible for integrating data from multiple internal and external sources, building reporting dashboards, producing actionable insights, and translating financial and operational data into recommendations that support improved dispute outcomes. This role requires strong data management, healthcare finance, reimbursement, and reporting capabilities, as well as the ability to connect claim-level detail, dispute outcomes, provider behavior, QPA performance, market benchmarks, and financial reporting trends. The role partners with stakeholders to define requirements, develop scalable reporting and data processes, and apply advanced analytical techniques to identify trends, forecast outcomes, and drive business performance.

Job Duties

  • Analyzes complex datasets from multiple sources to identify trends, patterns, risks, and opportunities. Tracks performance across pre-IDR negotiation, open negotiation, arbitration, settlement, and post-award outcomes.
  • Designs, develop, and maintain reports, dashboards, and data solutions using tools such as Structured Query Language (SQL), Microsoft Excel, and SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS). Produces standard and ad hoc reporting for Director, Network Strategy, Finance, Operations and health plan stakeholders.
  • Translates business needs into reporting and analytical requirements; partner with stakeholders to deliver actionable insights.
  • Combines data from multiple internal and external sources, including claims, QPA data, IDR case tracking, negotiation records, provider data, financial reporting, market benchmarks, and third-part data sources.
  • Performs healthcare data analysis, including claims, utilization, and cost data. Leverages external data sources as well to inform trends.
  • Develops and maintains data processes for extraction, transformation, validation, and integration.
  • Ensures data accuracy, integrity, and consistency through quality assurance and validation processes. Reconciles data across systems and identifies gaps, inconsistencies, and quality issues.
  • Partners with IT, Finance, Medical Economics, Actuary and Operations / Shared Services and external vendors to improve data availability and reporting automation, specifically collaborating with the provider dispute intake team
  • Produces and monitors key performance metrics, including: Percent of cases settled pre-IDR, averaged negotiated rate versus initial offer, percent of negotiations escalated to IDR, provider acceptance rate, IDR award versus QPA, IDR win rate, win rate by arbitrator, etc. Supports target-setting and performance management of dispute-related KPIs; establishes reporting views by market, state, provider, specialty, and arbitrator.
  • Develops financial views that quantifies dispute exposure, settlement impact, arbitration outcomes and avoided cost; translates financial reporting outputs into actionable insights for negotiation strategy and health plan playbooks
  • Develops visual dashboards that summarize OON dispute performance, financial impact, and strategic opportunities; creates executive-ready reporting materials for leadership reviews and governance forums; develops drill-down capability from enterprise-level performance to market, provider, specialty and case-level detail
  • Presents findings and recommendations to leadership and cross-functional teams.

Job Qualifications

  • At least 4 years of experience in data analysis, reporting, or analytics, or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
  • Strong experience with Structured Query Language (SQL), relational databases, and Microsoft Excel.
  • Experience with reporting and visualization tools (e.g., SQL Server Reporting Services (SSRS) or similar).
  • Experience working with complex datasets, including claims, provider, reimbursement, and financial data
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver on deadlines
  • Advanced data analysis and critical thinking, with experience developing dashboards, scorecards, recurring reports, and executive-facing analytics
  • Data quality & governance
  • Stakeholder communication & influence, with ability to translate detailed data into clear business insights and recommendations
  • Proficiency with data visualization and analytics tools, such as Tableau, Power BI, or other similar platforms

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience with No Surprises Act IDR, state-based provider dispute processes, OON claims, or provider payment disputes
    Knowledge of QPA methodology, provider reimbursement, Medicare-based pricing, commercial benchmarks, or payer claims adjudication
  • Experience combining internal data with external market data sources
  • Advanced SQL, Python R, or Alteryx skills
  • Experience with financial reporting, medical cost reporting, or healthcare P&L analysis
  • Experience supporting provider contracting, network strategy, medical economics, or payment integrity teams

Technical Direction & Architecture

  • Lead the engineering of scalable, high-performance, reliable distributed systems for the ValueLink squad.

Leadership, Mentoring & Communication

Government Compliance Coordinator

JOB SUMMARY
The Compliance Coordinator coordinates with various business partners on behalf of SCS Government Contract Compliance to support affiliate companies’ compliance with Davis-Bacon Act (DBA), Davis-Bacon Related Acts (DBRA), other prevailing wage requirements and other government contract compliance requirements applicable to federal contracts, financial assistance awards, loan guarantee agreements, and other federally funded/assisted construction activities/awards.

  • Assist business partners in the Southern system and SCS Government Contracts Compliance Manager in full lifecycle of contract and financial assistance administration including the preparation and review of government contract and financial assistance proposals, and post-award administration to assure compliance with government contract statutes and regulations and federal contract/agreement terms and conditions (including reporting and administrative requirements).
  • Serve as a point of contact for DBA/DBRA compliance support and coordination activities for covered federal contracts, financial assistance awards, loan guarantee agreements, and related project activities.
  • Assist business partners and project teams with implementation of applicable Davis-Bacon requirements, including wage determinations, labor standards obligations, certified payroll expectations, posting requirements, and related compliance processes.
  • Coordinate DBRA compliance activities across multiple projects and phases, including planning, procurement, contract development, construction, monitoring/oversight, reporting, and closeout.
  • Review labor standards requirements, contractor payroll submissions, contractor documentation, compliance records, and other project deliverables for completeness and consistency with applicable requirements.
  • Monitor project-level DBRA risks, open items, non-submissions, correction needs, and compliance trends; escalate material issues as appropriate.

  • Assist in the development, maintenance, and delivery of DBRA guidance, procedures, reference materials, training resources, and best practices for internal stakeholders and external partners.
  • Maintain accurate compliance records, reporting metrics, project and various DBA/DBRA monitoring and covered contract trackers, and documentation needed to support audits, reviews, management reporting, and contract or award/project construction closeout activities.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Accounting, Finance, Construction Management, Project Management, Public Administration, or other related technical field preferred; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of DOL labor standards requirements and federal agency management.

  • Highly effective written and oral communication skills, including the ability to communicate with all levels and disciplines of the business areas supported.
  • Strong attention to detail, documentation discipline, and ability to maintain accurate records in support of audits, reporting, and compliance reviews.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to coordinate effectively with Legal, Supply Chain Management, Payroll, Human Resources, project management, contractors, subcontractors, and government stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, identify compliance risks, and escalate issues appropriately.

Behavioral Attributes

  • Self-motivated, customer focused, and able to work with a strong sense of urgency.
  • Promotes teamwork and builds productive working relationships across functions and operating companies.

jobs.title: Senior Associate, Revenue Operations (Payer Operations)
jobs.excerpt: At Sword, we’re building AI to heal billions and unlock humanity’s full potential.
jobs.description:
At Sword, we’re building AI to heal billions and unlock humanity’s full potential. In doing so, we’re pioneering AI Care, a fundamentally new approach to healthcare built for medical reasoning, safety, and real-time treatment, not generic technology applied after the fact. As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Backed by 42 clinical studies, 44+ patents, and more than $500 million raised from leading investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, and Founders Fund, Sword is defining a new standard for healthcare.

AI Proficiency at Sword

AI fluency is a core expectation at Sword. Every candidate is assessed against our three-level framework — be ready to share real examples of how AI is already part of how you work.

  • Explorer (Level 1) — Uses AI daily to boost personal productivity

  • Builder (Level 2) — Creates workflows and tools that elevate the whole team

  • Integrator (Level 3) — Embeds AI into products and processes at scale

Every hire must demonstrate at least Level 1. The expected level will vary depending on the seniority of the role.

Role

We are looking for a seasoned revenue cycle operator who brings deep, hands-on mental and behavioral health billing expertise and is ready to own the revenue cycle end-to-end. This is not a role for someone who needs a well-scoped ticket queue. You will take the lead on moderately complex, loosely-defined problems, put durable processes in place where none exist today, and carry projects from inception through execution largely on your own.

Behavioral health reimbursement is its own discipline — EAP arrangements, session-based benefit limits, authorization requirements, and payer behavior that rarely resembles medical claims. We are looking for someone who has lived in that world and can act as our subject matter expert from day one. As the function grows, there may be a path for this person to take on oversight of a small team, and we are looking for someone who is interested in potentially growing into people leadership — you do not need management experience today, but you should be open to it tomorrow.

We are seeking an individual who thrives working cross-functionally and is passionate about digging into Product, Commercial and Operational processes that tie directly to product monetization. You will be instrumental in organization-wide initiatives related to profitability operations, and in replacing manual, error-prone processes with ones that scale. We want someone who thinks creatively about how to leverage AI to improve how the team works, and who is resourceful about the operational improvements that accelerate cash collections. In summary, we are looking for a self-starter who craves a challenge, moves fast, and questions the status quo — someone who can see the big picture but is equally willing to roll up their sleeves and get their hands dirty. Startup experience is preferred but not a must. The ideal candidate will have experience in health tech, behavioral health, or a provider organization with meaningful behavioral health volume.

Team

This role sits within the Finance organization and reports into the Senior Director of Revenue Operations (RevOps). The RevOps team is a small but mighty group with a strong growth mindset, who love working cross-functionally and are passionate about helping our members. This team is critical to the path to profitability and takes pride in working on high-visibility, high-stakes projects within the Finance organization. As a Senior Associate you will be one of the most independent operators on the team, trusted to own your scope outright and to raise the bar for those around you.

What you'll be doing:

  • Independently own pre-submission, submission and post-submission workflows across the revenue cycle — billing, claim scrubbing, rejections, denials, underpayments, recoupments, reconciliation and A/R follow-up — driving timely resolution and cash acceleration
  • Take the lead on directing and delivering timely solutions to moderately complex, loosely-scoped problems aligned to team and company goals, across all billing matters
  • Independently put processes, SOPs and SLA standards in place that improve the efficiency, consistency and quality of revenue cycle operations
  • Identify systemic trends and root causes in denials and payer behavior, and partner cross-functionally to drive durable fixes rather than recurring rework
  • Own leadership-facing reporting on RCM performance — collection rate, A/R days, denial and write-off rates, yield — and clearly communicate trends, root causes, and the changes, support or resourcing needed to improve outcomes
  • Identify and implement opportunities to leverage AI and automation to reduce manual operations and accelerate external cash collections
  • Work cross-functionally with Accounting and FP&A on month-end close activities
  • Enable Analysts on the team to be successful through mentoring, training and onboarding support, with the opportunity to oversee a small team as the function scales
  • Partner with our Intelligence, Data and Product teams to build quarterly roadmaps that align with company-wide goals
  • Develop self-serve dashboards that better support Commercial teams and eliminate the need for manual data manipulation
  • Work regularly with the Product team on scaling our home-grown billing tooling, and support billing system migrations and implementations end-to-end — requirements, configuration, testing and cutover
  • Work closely with Customer Success and Partner Success on all items related to customer and partner pricing, billing and payment; support the project management of setting up new payment structures as we expand into additional solutions
  • Own the front-end of the billing lifecycle, including participating in external calls with clients, payers and health plans, representing the company as the reimbursement SME
  • Support internal and external audits related to revenue cycle operations — ensuring readiness and compliance, and translating findings into durable process improvements
  • Enable Analysts and Associates on the team to be successful through mentoring, training and onboarding support
  • Ensure all billing processes and workflows adhere to HIPAA and applicable regulatory and industry standards

What you need to have:

  • Startup or high-growth company experience
  • Direct, hands-on experience billing mental and behavioral health services. You should be fluent in behavioral health claims, EAP billing and reauthorization, session-based benefit and clinical package tracking, prior authorizations, and the payer rules and authorization requirements specific to mental health services
  • At least 3.5 years of hands-on Revenue Cycle Management experience
  • Strong command of the medical claims lifecycle front to back, payer rules, and A/R management best practices
  • Demonstrated track record of independently owning projects from initiation through execution
  • An interest in growing into people leadership. Prior management experience is not required, but you should want to manage and potentially develop a small team over time.
  • Experience using data and reporting to drive operational decisions and performance improvements
  • Advanced Excel/Gsheet skills
  • Comfort with ambiguity and loosely-scoped problems
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Experience working cross-functionally with different teams, and the ability to influence stakeholders outside your reporting line
  • Efficient written and verbal communication skills
  • Excitement to wear multiple "hats" and problem solve effectively
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment
  • Undergraduate college degree

What we would love to see:

  • Experience in behavioral health, telehealth, or digital health environments at scale
  • Experience implementing process automation, RPA, or technology-enabled workflow improvements within RCM
  • Experience leading or supporting a billing system migration or implementation
  • Exposure to Medicare/CMS products, delegated credentialing, or payer contracting
  • Prior experience mentoring, training or informally leading teammates
  • We'd love to see someone who is self-motivated, resourceful and proactive about driving projects to success. Someone who is highly attentive to detail, has a learn-it-all attitude, and isn't afraid to ask questions, take on a new challenge and grow with Sword

*The range below reflects base, variable, and equity for this role.

This is a starting point, not a ceiling — once someone joins and proves they're outlier talent, we adjust quickly to make sure their compensation matches their impact.

Job titles may span more than one career level, so actual pay depends on skills, qualifications, experience, location, and market demand, among other factors. The range reflects base salary plus any variable, bonus, or sales incentives, and our estimate of the value of private company stock options where applicable. It's subject to change, and future stock value isn't guaranteed. Sword also offers additional benefits beyond total compensation.

Total Compensation Range
$108,500—$170,500 USD
Country-specific benefits may vary and will be detailed separately.

Who are we?
We are a female-founded scale-up, currently made up of around 100 AltoVitians. Our fully-remote team hails from 26 different countries and collectively speaks 29 languages. Most of the time, it is our differences that are celebrated (whether they are in cultures, personalities, preferences or passions). However, despite those differences, there are a few principal attributes that we share which define an AltoVitian. AltoVitians are tenacious, humble, and thoughtful. Being humble is important because it enables us to keep learning every day, and tenacity is necessary because in a high performing environment as fast-paced as AltoVita, taking it slow is simply not an option!

As we look to scale our Global Commercial engine, today is a particularly exciting time to join our team. This next chapter won’t always be a smooth ride, but it will be filled with innovation, excitement and opportunities. If you are ambitious, commercially hungry and ready for the challenge (and the fun!) of growing with us, we would love to hear from you.

What we do

AltoVita is a multi-award winning accommodation platform that enables enterprises to consolidate accommodation programmes through the power of proprietary technology paired with a human centric approach.

AltoVita’s unique offering sets us apart in the market, providing a network of 10 million+ verified and vetted properties are all duty of care compliant, backed by a four-tier quality control process; located in over 35,000 cities & 165 countries world-wide. With our award-winning enterprise software and human-centric approach, we deliver smart and sustainable solutions to global talent mobility & business travel managers worldwide.

Our Client Development team plays a vital role as trusted advisors and partners to our clients. Embodying our consultative philosophy, this dedicated team proactively shares new market insights, analyzes data, and empowers our clients with the tools and knowledge to make informed decisions, ensuring our clients are always equipped to make the best choices for their corporate housing needs.

AltoVita’s technology provides a cloud-based bridge between the highly fragmented property distribution system and multinational Global 2000 companies. A proprietary two-way API integration with a standardized sourcing process reduces the legacy, inefficient 48-to-72-hour bidding process down to a few minutes, saving valuable time and money.

Corporate clients love the bespoke user interface seamlessly configured to their mobility policies, and employees enjoy a greater sense of choice and support in their relocation journey.

About the role

The Director of Sales, US, will support AltoVita's Sales and Business Development efforts in the region, reporting into the SVP Sales, US. This is an external facing role focused on building credible relationships, opening doors with new prospects, and creating qualified opportunities.

This is a mid-level opportunity for someone ambitious, commercially hungry, and highly coachable, with real potential to grow into a more senior sales role at AltoVita as you prove yourself.

The Sales Director, US, will be measured on revenue related KPI’s and will share responsibility and accountability for the success of AltoVita’s sales efforts in the region. Please note, this role will be based in the US and you must have relevant work history. Please only apply if you have demand side experience, not supply side.

Your Responsibilities will be to:

  • Identify new business opportunities within the US, including new markets, growth areas, trends, customers, and services.

  • Build a well diversified pipeline of qualified opportunities by seeking out the right contacts within target organisations and generating leads through outreach and cold calling, maintaining a strong weekly meeting cadence.

  • Learn, master and fluently demonstrate AltoVita’s technology, including the AltoVerse product suite, across all verticals and stages of the sales pipeline.

  • Consistently elevate AltoVita’s brand awareness through thought leadership, LinkedIn presence, and hosting high-impact webinars, roundtables and industry events.

  • Work with the Marketing team to support lead acquisition and nurturing.

  • Leverage your network to build genuine, credible relationships with prospective clients, employees, and other stakeholders, bringing a client centric, “above and beyond” mindset to how you serve them.

  • Meet with prospects face to face or virtually, and attend relevant conferences and industry events to build AltoVita's presence in the market, planning travel efficiently to maximize ROI.

  • Act as a trusted first point of contact, earning credibility and open doors that convert into qualified sales opportunities.

  • Keep abreast of trends and changes in relocation, business travel, hospitality, corporate housing, and serviced apartment industries.

  • Develop, forecast, and report on your sales funnel whilst demonstrating full accountability, keeping CRM and documentation accurate and up to date.

  • Optimize travel between the region to maximize sales efforts and minimize expenses.

  • Clearly and consistently communicate pipeline progress to your line managers and internal stakeholders.

  • Collaborate with the Product and Client Development teams to feed back client needs and market learnings.

  • Hand off qualified opportunities to the enablement/closing team at the right stage, ensuring a smooth transition and a clear client handover.

  • Learn and upscale to new verticals and geographies that are important for the company.

What you will bring:

  • Core: strategic thinking, innovation, sound decision making, strong collaboration & communication, comfort with change, agility, and a client-centric mindset.
  • Leadership: ownership & accountability, resource and performance management, and a track record of developing others (as your book of business and any team grow).
  • Meta: a strong learning orientation, critical thinking & problem solving, and adaptability & resilience.

Who you are:

  • 3+ years in (external) sales in the US region

  • 3+ years experience within the business travel or corporate housing industry

  • Tenacious and driven

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, sometimes less structured and entrepreneurial environment

  • Able to think strategically

Ways of Working

AltoVita is a fully remote team. Although we have regular touch-points throughout the week, organize off-sites in several locations, trust is essential for us to work effectively as a team. Our founders empower us to make decisions autonomously, and in turn expect that we also empower our direct reports.

Join our Team

AltoVita is the sum of every member of the team. We know that a strong team is a diverse team, and are therefore committed to being an equal opportunity employer, so please bring all of yourself to the interviews and most importantly to our team.

Becoming an AltoVitian means you will benefit from:

  • A team that will always put you first

  • Incredible opportunities for growth and career advancement

  • A fully-remote working environment

  • Wellness benefits and a wellness budget, which can be spent on a range of options including gym memberships, home meal delivery services, mindfulness applications, and many more

  • A work-from-home allowance to get your home-office set up

  • A generous vacation package so you can recharge or explore

jobs.description:
Covetrus is a global animal-health technology and services leader dedicated to empowering veterinary practice partners to drive improved health and financial outcomes. We bring together products, services, and technology into a single platform that connects our customers to the solutions and insights they need to work best. Our passion for the well-being of animals and those who care for them drives us to advance the world of veterinary medicine.



The Business Unit Controller is responsible for the oversight of the accounting, financial reporting, and control environment of Covetrus North America’s largest business unit. The MWI Controller will leverage their accounting expertise in revenue recognition, inventory management and other complex areas such as software development, property accounting, internal controls, process implementation and operational oversight.


The Controller will have an in-depth knowledge of US GAAP and will have the ability to apply standard principles, theories, concepts and techniques as well as make complex decisions. As a core leader of the Controllership team, this role is responsible for inspiring the team, peers, and leadership, and building an effective and engaged team while supporting their development.

This position reports to the North America Controller and manages a team of accounting professionals.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Direct the functional areas within revenue recognition, inventory control, general accounting, and compliance through partnership with various areas of operations, FP&A and shared services.
  • Ensure compliance with GAAP and other regulatory and/or internally developed accounting policies and procedures.
  • Oversee monthly accounting close process including analytical review of the monthly results to ensure accurate accounting records are maintained.
  • Serve as the point of contact and owner of key controls that include, but not limited to: record to report, procure to pay, order to cash, leasing, inventory, and fixed assets.
  • Be attuned to early warnings of financial control gaps and be able to proactively implement action plans to swiftly remedy.
  • Understand and manage multiple different income streams including product, manufacturing, fees, subscription, software, royalty, consulting, bundling, rebates and margin reimbursements.
  • Provide thought leadership to the business on revenue building initiatives while ensuring compliance with revenue recognition (ASC 606)
  • Comfortable creating or re-evaluating current policies and memos around reserves and impairment analyses that can vary across subsidiaries.
  • Oversight of all intercompany transactions and allocation methodologies.
  • Oversight of all physical inventories and material cycle count adjustments and ensure compliance based on established controls.
  • Implement, document and maintain adequate and effective processes to improve and shorten the monthly accounting close.
  • Issue timely and complete month-end reports and analytics to the consolidation team.
  • Serve as the point of contact for all internal and external audits.
  • Provide counsel and advice to management in developing objectives, strategies and tactics from a financial and accounting perspective.
  • Encourage ideas and creative approaches for continuous improvement.
  • Establish a clear understanding of other functional areas of company and provide guidance to executives of Business Development, Operations, Quality, HR, Program Management, Product, and Development in relation to financial goals and strategies.
  • Keep up to date on the animal health market and applicable accounting rules and regulations.
  • Provide training and guidance to finance staff and non-financial colleagues across the business.
  • Mentor/develop direct reports and retain/promote top performers.

QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLSETS

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance
  • CPA Required, MBA a plus
  • 8+ years of diverse financial experience in various finance / accounting roles
  • 3+ years in a hands-on management position
  • Strength of character, with the ability to take clear, decisive action in steering the company's worth and safeguard values
  • A history of active involvement and success beyond the traditional responsibilities of financial reporting
  • Experience integrating an accounting function as part of a business combination
  • Works effectively in a fast-paced environment with multiple competing deadlines
  • Possess agility and can adapt quickly to changing priorities
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Strong work ethic with willingness and ability to dig into details to accomplish tasks and complete projects
