Manager, Product Operations

SaiSystems Health | Product Organization | Reports to CPO

What You'll Do

  • Own the strategy, roadmap, and continuous improvement of the tools and workflows that power the Product team's experience — including Aha!, Confluence, and Pendo — and partner with Engineering on how those tools connect to Jira and release infrastructure.
  • Build and manage the product analytics stack, ensuring Product Managers have reliable access to usage data, feature adoption metrics, and customer behavior insights through Pendo and related tools.
  • Develop and run enablement programs for the Product team — onboarding new PMs, rolling out new tools and methodologies, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.
  • Define and track product-team operational health metrics (process adoption, time-to-insight, PM ramp time, roadmap-to-delivery traceability) and use them to identify bottlenecks and improvement opportunities.
  • Partner with Engineering leadership and the Release Manager on delivery standards, tooling investments, and how release readiness and cadence decisions surface to the Product team.
  • Evaluate and recommend new tools, integrations, and AI-assisted workflows that increase Product team productivity and decision-making quality.
  • Directly manage the APM team — providing coaching, performance feedback, and career development support, and coordinating their work to drive consistency across product delivery.

What You Bring

  • 3-5 years of experience in product operations, product management, program management, or a related role in a software or healthcare IT organization.
  • Working knowledge of Jira from a Product Manager's/reporting perspective (boards, filters, dashboards); deep administrative configuration is not required.
  • Experience with product analytics platforms (Pendo, Amplitude, or similar) and a strong understanding of how to interpret usage data.
  • Proven ability to design and implement scalable processes that work across multiple product lines.
  • Strong communication and facilitation skills — able to drive alignment across PMs, engineers, and leadership.
  • Comfort with AI-assisted tooling and a forward-looking perspective on how AI can improve product team workflows.
  • Experience in healthcare IT is a plus but not required.

How You Lead

  • You are a systems thinker who sees the connections between tools, processes, and team performance.
  • You lead by making others more effective — your success is measured by how well the Product team operates.
  • You are data-driven and operationally rigorous, but you balance process with pragmatism.
  • You are a builder, not just a maintainer — you proactively design new workflows and systems rather than waiting for requests.
  • You mentor and develop your team, treating operational excellence as a craft worth investing in.

Why This Role Matters

Product Operations ensures every PM and designer at SaiSystems Health has the tools, data, and processes they need to do their best work, and that the Product team's practices scale as the organization grows.

In doing so, we’re pioneering AI Care, a fundamentally new approach to healthcare built for medical reasoning, safety, and real-time treatment, not generic technology applied after the fact. As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Backed by 42 clinical studies, 44+ patents, and more than $500 million raised from leading investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, and Founders Fund, Sword is defining a new standard for healthcare.

AI Proficiency at Sword

AI fluency is a core expectation at Sword. Every candidate is assessed against our three-level framework — be ready to share real examples of how AI is already part of how you work.

  • Explorer (Level 1) — Uses AI daily to boost personal productivity

  • Builder (Level 2) — Creates workflows and tools that elevate the whole team

  • Integrator (Level 3) — Embeds AI into products and processes at scale

Every hire must demonstrate at least Level 1. The expected level will vary depending on the seniority of the role.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Ensure AI agents perform consistently before and after going live;
  • Monitor performance across different healthcare environments and languages;
  • Liaise with the clinical team to create protocols and understand what clinically relevant parameters should be monitored;
  • Establish quality standards that work for AI systems, not traditional software;
  • Fix the underlying prompt logic and reasoning chains;
  • Create new testing methods to prevent similar issues;
  • Figure out how to test systems designed to be intelligent and adaptive;
  • Build frameworks for testing across infinite healthcare scenarios;
  • Define what "good enough" means for AI in healthcare;
  • Manage compliance with MDR (Medical Device Regulation) and AI Act requirements for AI systems together with the compliance team;
  • Document quality processes and verification and validation procedures for regulatory submissions;
  • Help ensure the algorithms perform with the expected accuracy and do not lead to bias;
  • Work with compliance teams to achieve and maintain certification of the relevant algorithms;
  • Help establish industry standards for AI quality assurance;
  • Become one of the few experts in AI healthcare testing methodologies;
  • Build your expertise in a field that's just being created;

What you need to have:

  • Comfortable speaking and understanding English (doesn't need to be perfect);
  • 2-6 years of experience in QA, testing, or analytical roles;
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills;
  • Comfortable learning new technologies and methodologies;
  • Curious about the evolving AI landscape;

What we would love to see:

  • Familiarity with secure handling of health data (GDPR, HIPAA);
  • Experience with medical device regulations (MDR, 21 CFR 820, ISO 13485, IEC62304);
  • Comfortable speaking and understanding Portuguese;
  • Experience with AI tools or prompt engineering;
  • Background in healthcare, enterprise software, or regulated industries;
  • Familiarity with quality metrics and monitoring systems;
  • Basic programming or scripting experience.

*The range below reflects base, variable, and equity for this role.

This is a starting point, not a ceiling — once someone joins and proves they're outlier talent, we adjust quickly to make sure their compensation matches their impact.

We are a staffing agency hiring on behalf of a residential property management company located in Seminole, Florida, serving the greater Tampa Bay area (including St. Petersburg, Clearwater, and Largo)

We are looking for an experienced, highly organized, and communicative Maintenance Coordinator to manage and streamline property maintenance operations.

This is a hands-on position for a proactive professional with practical experience in property management and maintenance coordination. You will serve as the primary point of contact between tenants, property managers, and vendors—ensuring maintenance issues and work orders are clearly communicated, efficiently scheduled, and cost-effectively resolved.

You will take full ownership of the maintenance workflow, driving issue resolution, managing vendor relationships, and ensuring a seamless experience for both property owners and tenants.

Key Responsibilities

  • Work Order Management: Receive, triage, and manage property maintenance requests and work orders from intake through to successful completion.

  • Tenant & Stakeholder Communication: Clearly explain work order details, timelines, expectations, and resolution steps to tenants with empathy, clarity, and professionalism.

  • AppFolio System Operations: Maintain real-time accurate logs, records, updates, and documentation within AppFolio.

  • Vendor Negotiation & Cost Control: Actively negotiate and push back on vendor pricing to ensure fair rates, accurate scopes of work, and high-quality deliverables.

  • Vendor Sourcing & Onboarding: Continuously explore, vet, and onboard new service providers and contractors to build a robust, competitive vendor network.

  • Scheduling & Dispatching: Coordinate access with tenants and schedule contractors/vendors for timely property visits and repairs.

  • Invoice & Quality Auditing: Review work completion reports, audit vendor invoices against original quotes, and approve for payment.

Requirements

The successful candidate will have:

  • AppFolio Expertise:Essential. Demonstrable hands-on experience using AppFolio for property management and maintenance operations.

  • Exceptional Communication: Outstanding verbal and written English communication skills, with the ability to handle delicate tenant conversations and firm vendor discussions.

  • Strong Negotiation Skills: Proven track record of negotiating pricing, reviewing job scopes, and holding vendors accountable.

  • Organizational Mastery: Superb attention to detail, strong multi-tasking capabilities, and the ability to manage high-volume daily requests efficiently.

  • Property Maintenance Knowledge: solid understanding of residential property maintenance issues, trade terminology, and standard repair timelines.

  • Problem-Solving Skills: Strong troubleshooting capabilities to assess issues accurately before dispatching vendors.

This is not an entry-level role. We are looking for someone who has previously worked in property management coordination and can hit the ground running.

Working Style

You should be comfortable working independently and taking ownership of your workload in a fast-paced environment.

We will provide clear operational guidelines, but you are expected to take initiative, resolve conflicts proactively, and drive tasks across the finish line without requiring constant step-by-step supervision.

The right person will be:

  • Reliable, highly organized, and detail-oriented

  • A firm yet diplomatic communicator who is comfortable having tough conversations with tenants or vendors

  • Solution-focused with strong critical-thinking skills

  • Able to prioritize competing demands under pressure

  • Proactive in identifying cost-saving opportunities and discovering new vendor partners

  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment

jobs.excerpt: We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity.
jobs.description:
We are excited to speak to you about this opportunity. If you are interested in joining our growing team, please apply to this link directly.

Who we are

At Aquila, we invest in category-defining B2B/B2G software companies globally, acting as a thought-partner, striving for the success of our companies in the long term. We are a well-managed, profitable company that operates like a startup with the financial backing of a parent company. For our people, this means limitless possibilities.

We are unapologetically unique, pivoting to respond to the needs of the multiple markets we operate in. We have ambitious goals, and we are looking for genuine contributors with integrity, energy, flexibility, and loyalty. We are investing in building future leaders who can take an idea and make things happen.

Who we need

GIFTSOFT and Cibar provide specialized financial technology solutions that help financial institutions manage bank to bank payments, anti-money-laundering, trade finance and other complex financial operations. Together, and backed by Constellation Software, they combine deep industry expertise with technology designed to improve efficiency, manage risk, and modernize critical banking processes.

Reporting to the Aquila Portfolio Manager, we are hiring a Business Development Representative to create new sales opportunities for GIFTSOFT and Cibar. You will utilize the latest in AI and tooling to research financial institutions, identify the right contacts, and start relevant conversations with prospective clients. Representing each business, you will build an understanding of their solutions, generate interest, and connect qualified prospects with the appropriate sales expert.

This is a full-time, fully remote position.

What’s in it for you

Ownership and influence. This is a newly created role and a new approach to business development across the portfolio. You will work closely with the Portfolio Manager and the leaders in each business to shape how the role operates, from prospecting processes and ways of working to how activity and success are measured. As the model develops, your experience and insights will help inform how similar business development roles may be introduced across other businesses.

Broader sales opportunities. Working across GIFTSOFT and Cibar gives you two distinct sets of solutions and a broader range of prospective clients and conversations to pursue. You will gain exposure to payments, fraud, compliance, and global trade finance technology while developing your ability to identify where each offering can create value for financial institutions.

Career growth. You will have the opportunity to build on your business development experience in a role with larger accounts, complex sales cycles, and senior decision-makers. Working alongside experienced sales professionals across two businesses, you will deepen your understanding of enterprise software sales and build the skills and industry knowledge to take on more of the sales cycle as you grow. This role has the potential to grow into a direct selling role if successful.

How you will make an impact

  • Open new doors. You will research financial institutions (primarily banks) and identify new prospects for both GIFTSOFT and Cibar, finding the right contacts, recognizing relevant business triggers, and creating opportunities to start conversations.
  • Prospect strategically. You will be an user of Apollo and other sales and AI-enabled tools to research accounts, identify contacts, personalize outreach, build targeted prospect lists and manage campaigns. You will combine these insights with your own judgment to determine who to approach, what will resonate, and how best to earn their attention.
  • Start meaningful conversations. You will connect with prospective clients through phone, email, LinkedIn, and other channels, introducing the GIFTSOFT or Cibar solution most relevant to their needs. You will tailor your approach to different stakeholders, priorities, and business challenges to create interest and open the door to further discussion.
  • Qualify and connect. You will develop enough knowledge of both businesses to confidently introduce their solutions, ask thoughtful questions, and recognize where there may be a fit. You will qualify genuine opportunities and connect prospects with the appropriate sales expert for deeper discovery and next steps.
  • Help build the playbook. As one of the first people in this shared BDR model, you will work with the business unit leaders, sales and the Portfolio Manager to refine target accounts, messaging, outreach strategies, qualification criteria, and measures of success. You will use activity and outcomes to understand what is working and help shape a repeatable approach that can evolve across the portfolio.

You bring

  • The hunter mindset. You enjoy opening doors that are not already open. You are motivated by prospecting, comfortable with cold outreach, persistent when response rates are low, and energized by turning an unknown account into a genuine sales conversation.
  • The outbound experience. You have experience generating new business through outbound calls, email, LinkedIn, or other prospecting channels. You understand that effective business development requires research, consistency, thoughtful follow-up, and the ability to handle rejection without losing momentum.
  • The AI fluency. You are comfortable using AI-powered prospecting and productivity tools to research accounts, find contacts, personalize messaging, and work more efficiently. You know how to assess and refine AI-generated information rather than simply relying on the output.
  • The communication skills. You can speak confidently with stakeholders at different levels and adjust your approach depending on who you are engaging. You know how to create enough interest in an initial conversation to earn the next one without being the product expert.
  • The curiosity and learning agility. You are comfortable learning new products, industries, and customer environments. Experience in B2B SaaS, fintech, banking, payments, trade finance, or enterprise technology helps, but demonstrated outbound capability and a strong desire to learn matter more.
  • Nurturing relationships. You build genuine rapport with stakeholders across different levels and take a long-term approach to trust-building, ensuring strong connections throughout the sales cycle.
  • Number and target oriented. You are driven by goals, metrics, and outcomes. You thrive on meeting or exceeding targets and consistently track activity to drive performance.

Why join?

GIFTSOFT, Cibar, and Aquila are part of Constellation Software Inc., one of Canada's largest and most successful software companies and its most successful technology stock over the last 10 years [TSE: CSU].

Our entrepreneurial culture, lean environment, and people come together to form a dynamic organization where purpose drives our growth. This is a place where high performance and hard work are rewarded, where leaders are grown, and where the best ideas win. With the autonomy to be creative and curious, we collaborate and iterate to achieve real impact in the communities we support.

We spend our days asking questions and challenging the status quo, manipulating our structure, roles, and internal operations in order to stay ahead in a competitive landscape.

If you share our growth mindset, relationship-focused approach, and high moral fibre, you will thrive at Aquila.

Compensation

Compensation is structured around experience, with a $50,000–$80,000 base and $80,000–$110,000 in total OTE.

Apply now.

Diversity and inclusion are not mere words on paper to us. We welcome and appreciate candidates with a range of backgrounds and experiences. If you have most of the qualifications we are seeking, and want to play an integral role in our success, apply to express your interest.

What you can expect from our interview process:

  • A virtual interview with a Talent Advisor will be scheduled to discuss your interest in the role and share your relevant experience. The conversation will be recorded using BrightHire, an AI-powered video interview tool. More details will be shared when you are invited to interview.
  • A virtual interview with the Creative Marketing Manager and Chief Revenue Officer, focused on your outbound sales experience, approach to lead generation, use of AI and sales technology, communication skills, and ability to engage different stakeholders.
  • A virtual interview with the Portfolio Manager, focused on your approach to business development, hunter mindset, learning agility, and potential to grow within the portfolio.
  • A virtual introduction to the business unit leaders of both Cibar and GIFTSOFT.

jobs.description:
Purpose of the role

We are looking for an engineer who knows the broadcast and video world in depth and can turn that knowledge into reliable software. You will be our go-to person for video formats, codecs, and broadcast-specific media handling within our MAM platform. You will work in a team on Kubernetes-based, GitOps-delivered services, with architectural guidance from our senior architects.

Responsibilities

  • Implement and maintain media-handling features: ingest, analysis, transcoding, proxy generation, and delivery in broadcast-grade formats.
  • Analyze and resolve format-related issues (non-conformant files, interlace/frame-rate problems, audio channel mapping, timecode and metadata errors).
  • Integrate and tune transcoders and media tools (e.g. FFmpeg, MediaInfo, commercial transcoding engines) in containerized workflows.
  • Map and validate technical and descriptive metadata against broadcast standards and customer specifications.
  • Support customer projects and escalations with media-domain expertise.
  • Contribute to code quality and security (SonarQube, Mend) and to CI/CD pipelines.
  • Document format and workflow knowledge so it spreads across the team.

Must-have

  • Hands-on experience in broadcast, post-production, or MAM environments.
  • Solid knowledge of the video formatsin everyday use:
    • Codecs: H.264/AVC, HEVC, MPEG-2, ProRes, DNxHD/DNxHR, XDCAM HD/IMX, AVC-Intra, JPEG 2000
    • Containers: MXF (OP1a, OPAtom), MP4/MOV, MPEG-TS, ideally IMF
    • Video fundamentals: interlaced vs. progressive, frame rates (incl. 29.97/59.94 and drop-frame timecode), aspect ratios, color spaces (BT.601/709/2020), basics of HDR (PQ/HLG)
    • Audio: channel layouts and mapping, sample rates, loudness (EBU R128)
  • Experience with media metadata and subtitle/caption formats (e.g. EBU Core, SMPTE, BWF, EBU-TT/STL, TTML, CEA-608/708).
  • Practical experience with FFmpeg and media analysis tooling.
  • Programming experience in [Java / .Net / C#] and comfort working with REST APIs.
  • Working knowledge of Kubernetes and Helm, plus Git-based workflows.
  • Structured, quality-conscious way of working; fluent English, German is a plus.

Tooling and stack

  • Platform: Kubernetes, Helm, GitOps (Flux or Argo CD)
  • Cloud: AWS (working knowledge: S3, EKS, IAM basics)
  • CI/CD: Azure DevOps, GitHub
  • Quality & security: SonarQube, Mend (day-to-day use, fixing findings)
  • Media tooling: FFmpeg, MediaInfo, MXF analysis tools
  • Nice to know: OpenTelemetry/Grafana for debugging media pipelines

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with Vidispine or similar MAM platforms (Avid, Dalet, Telestream, etc.)
  • Delivery specs such as AS-11 (UK DPP), IMF, or broadcaster-specific specifications (e.g. ARD/ZDF)
  • Knowledge of live and IP workflows (SMPTE ST 2110, SRT)
  • Experience with AI/ML-based media enrichment (speech-to-text, face/object detection)
  • Familiarity with AWS media services (MediaConvert, etc.)

Soft skills

  • Curious and detail-oriented, enjoys getting to the root cause of a broken file
  • Explains media topics clearly to engineers who are not broadcast experts
  • Reliable team player who takes ownership of their area and asks early when blocked

Overview

The Principal Product Architect will play a pivotal role in leading the design and architecture of scalable, secure, and highly available SaaS products, with an emphasis on public cloud design and deployment. This is a senior-level position requiring deep expertise in cloud technologies, SaaS models, and a proven track record of successful SaaS product deployment.

You will be responsible for defining the architectural vision, ensuring the scalability, security, and performance of products within your purview.

The Principal Product Architect partners with product management to ensure product roadmaps and release planning and align with the defined technology strategy. This role guides product engineering teams in the architecturally sound product design for public cloud, on-premises, and hybrid product deployments and maintains a product technology roadmap to achieve target state product alignment. This role focuses on technology assessments, proofs-of-concept, living architectural artifacts in the architecture governance lifecycle, and ensuring product design compliance with architecture, security, and operational standards.

This role provides thought leadership and, through the product technology roadmap, collaborates with product leadership to reconceive existing products to cloud native designs. This person engages with product engineering, technical architecture, security and operations to ensure compliance with reference product models.

The Principal Product Architect brings a blend of commercial SaaS product design, technical expertise, cross functional acumen, and translates complex requirements into actionable plans while promoting innovation, collaboration, and operational efficiency.

  • Architectural Strategy

  • Architects and implements cloud-native SaaS products that perform at scale. Designs and manages the architecture of complex, cloud and hybrid products for elasticity, availability, and resiliency.   • Innovation:

Qualifications

  • Advanced critical thinking and problem solving skills as demonstrated by the ability to listen, collect, data, and make successful recommendations
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to lead technical discussions and influence decision-making processes related to product architecture
  • Ability to cultivate internal relationships and effectively engage with technical and non-technical stakeholders, share insights, and drive innovation
  • Strong knowledge of the appropriate use of AWS services and awareness of AWS cost management and optimization strategies
  • Ability to apply cloud architecture principles, including scalability, high availability, data retention, disaster recovery, and security best practices.
  • Intermediate knowledge of utilizing compliance frameworks and regulations (e.g., HITRUST, HIPAA, SOC 2)
  • Familiarity with Identity and Access models in on-prem and public cloud
  • Advanced proficiency in cloud-native serverless application design and development, microservices architecture, and event driven design patterns
  • Strong experience with monitoring and observability tools, including AWS CloudWatch
  • Demonstrated practice of emotional intelligence that is used to work effectively in a deadline driven, agile environment
  • Expertise in cloud service design patterns and architectures, including multi-region and multi-tenant SaaS models

Experience

Preferred Experience

At NASCO, we trust our workforce to be fully remote, working from their home. This benefit offers significant, personalized outcomes for each associate including work/life balance, savings on commuting, work clothing, and increased time to spend on personal activities.

Other Benefits

The position is an entry level fraud investigator/auditor position expected to work under the direct supervision of a team manager and/or team lead. The team performs high level complex investigations of medical professional service providers and develops cases/reports for future action, including referral to law enforcement, education, over payment recovery and other administrative actions. This position will support the team of fraud investigators/auditors and will work with internal resources and external agencies to develop cases/audits and corrective actions as well as respond to requests for data and support.

  • The Investigator may also be required to assist in the completion of complex reports that apply regulations or rules to the program(s) affected by the behavior being reviewed.

jobs.description:
Overview

THE OPPORTUNITY

Every month, renters pay for housing through property management companies, and that relationship gives us something rare: a trusted, recurring, high-frequency touchpoint with the resident. We are building the financial layer around it: payments, insurance, rewards, embedded financial products and a resident AI that ties the experience together. Partners are how that layer gets built, funded and made valuable.

As Head of Partnerships you will be the single front door for every external relationship that matters to our fintech business: the banks and financial institutions that power our products, the fintechs and platforms that extend them, and the consumer brands that give residents a reason to engage. You will build the network, structure the deals, and run the relationships so that each partner creates measurable value for residents, for property managers and for us.

Responsibilities

WHAT YOU WILL OWN

  • Bank and financial institution partnerships. Own the relationships behind our money-movement and financial products: sponsor and issuing banks, BaaS providers, card networks and processors. Source, negotiate and manage them for resilience, economics and regulatory fit.
  • Embedded finance partnerships. Build the partner network behind embedded products such as loans, cards and other financial services, and structure revenue-share, funding and distribution models that work for both sides.
  • Resident-value partnerships. Source and sign consumer brands (streaming, mobility, retail, travel and more) that make the resident experience worth using, and shape offers that drive engagement and loyalty.
  • Strategic and existing partner relationships. Run the executive relationships with the strategic partners we already work with. Protect and grow volume, align roadmaps and manage performance, economics and renewals.
  • Deal structuring and governance. Lead commercial terms from first conversation to signature, with Legal, Finance, Risk and Compliance. Build a clear approval path, deal flow visibility and partner scorecards.
  • Partner activation. Great contracts are not enough. Work with Product, Resident Experience, Engineering and GTM so each partner launches on time, performs and scales.
  • Ecosystem strategy. Decide where we build, buy or partner. Bring a point of view on the fintech and bank landscape and where our resident ecosystem creates leverage.

HOW YOU WILL WORK

Partnerships succeeds when it works as one team with the rest of the business:

  • With Product and Engineering on partner requirements, integrations and roadmap trade-offs.
  • With Resident Experience on what residents actually want from a partner offer.
  • With GTM & Commercialization and Marketing on joint launches, co-marketing and adoption.
  • With Finance, Risk, Compliance and Legal on economics, diligence, regulatory fit and contracts.

Qualifications

WHAT YOU BRING

Demonstrable partnership results are the heart of this role. We are looking for someone who can show us, with names, deals and outcomes, what they built.

  • 10+ years in fintech business development and partnerships, with a record of originating, negotiating and closing material deals with banks, fintechs, processors or networks.
  • Hands-on experience structuring bank and BaaS partnerships (sponsor or issuing banks, card programs, lending or funding partners) and managing them through diligence, launch and steady state.
  • A track record building consumer or resident ecosystems: signing brand and benefit partners, designing offers, and showing the engagement or revenue they produced.
  • Deep command of embedded finance and partnership economics: revenue share, take rate, funding costs, risk sharing and unit economics.
  • Experience running executive-level relationships and managing a partner portfolio for performance, not just signing it.
  • Comfort in a regulated environment: you know what banks, compliance and risk teams need, and you bring them in early.
  • A real network across banks, fintechs and consumer brands that you can activate from day one.

Nice to have: multifamily, real estate or property technology exposure; marketplace or platform partnerships; experience building a partnerships function and team from scratch.

WHY JOIN

  • A partner proposition with real pull. A resident base reached through property managers, a growing set of financial products, and a roadmap that gives partners something unique to plug into.
  • Scope and visibility. A direct report to the Chief Fintech Officer, a seat on the leadership team, and a scorecard the board sees.
  • Build, don’t maintain. You will set the partnership strategy, the deal process and the team.
  • Impact you can measure. Each partnership connects to resident outcomes and the numbers we report to the board.

Pay Range

USD $157,600.00 - USD $286,400.00 /Yr.

Overview

We are looking for an Agentic AI Architect I to help design scalable, reliable, and reusable architectures for production-grade AI agents. You will work across product, engineering, AI Platform, infrastructure, QA/Eval, operations, and support teams to translate business and workflow requirements into practical agent architectures. Your work may span agent orchestration, runtime services, tool and system integrations, workflow execution, observability, evaluation, responsible AI controls, and production support.

This is a hands-on architecture role for someone who can balance technical design, implementation practicality, reliability, and delivery speed. The successful candidate will help teams avoid fragile one-off solutions by identifying reusable patterns that can be adopted across AI agent products.

Responsibilities

Primary Responsibilities

  • Design end-to-end architectures for agentic AI solutions, including orchestration, runtime execution, workflow management, tool invocation, system integrations, evaluation, observability, and supportability.
  • Translate product requirements, business workflows, and customer use cases into clear technical designs and implementation plans.
  • Define reusable patterns for multi-step agent behavior, task routing, handoffs, cross-system interactions, state management, and multi-agent coordination where appropriate.

  • Collaborate with engineering teams during implementation through architecture reviews, design guidance, technical documentation, and production-readiness assessments.

  • Partner with QA/Eval teams to incorporate evaluation criteria, regression coverage, testing strategies, and quality controls into agent architecture.
  • Support release planning, launch-readiness reviews, production monitoring, incident response, and post-release improvement.
  • Identify repeated solution patterns and recommend when they should become shared product or platform capabilities.
  • Contribute to architecture standards, reference designs, technical decision records, implementation guidance, and reusable documentation.
  • Help teams apply responsible AI, privacy, security, governance, and human oversight requirements throughout the solution lifecycle.
  • Communicate technical decisions, dependencies, risks, and recommendations clearly to engineering, product, operations, and business stakeholders.

Qualifications

  • Experience designing or building backend systems, distributed applications, workflow platforms, integration services, developer platforms, cloud applications, or AI-enabled solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing or implementing production LLM applications, AI agents, workflow automation, or intelligent assistant solutions.

jobs.description:
About Mainspring

Mainspring Energy manufactures and delivers fuel-flexible, low-emissions local power solutions that rapidly add new capacity and deliver reliable, affordable, and sustainable electric power. The company began commercial shipments of its Mainspring Linear Generators in 2020 and today has hundreds of megawatts in advanced development and field operations for leading Fortune 500 companies, data centers, and utilities. Mainspring also partners with global energy leaders including AEP, NextEra Energy Resources, Schneider Electric, and more.

The core values that ground our work, guide our decisions, and connect us together:

  • Pragmatic Optimism
  • Excellence without Ego
  • Proactive Collaboration

Job Overview

    Site Integration Engineers report to the Project Engineering Manager within the Project Delivery department. A key enabler of Mainspring’s mission is the ability of its team to deliver solutions based on our linear generator technology that solve customer problems in the cross-section of resiliency and clean power supply.

    The project engineering team provides the technical expertise, guidance, and support to deploy linear generators into the field efficiently—building customer confidence and enabling future scalability. This role owns site-level readiness after construction is complete, ensuring that all mechanical, electrical, control, and communication systems are fully integrated, validated, and ready to transition into commissioning and operation. Generator commissioning is performed by a separate team; this role ensures the site is ready for it. Acting as the technical integration authority on site, this role bridges engineering design intent and real-world system operation.

Responsibilities

    This role will be responsible for:

  • Interpreting technical project details, including scopes of work, sequences of operation, control narratives, and engineering drawings (site plans, P&IDs, single-line, and three-line diagrams), and serving as the controls subject matter expert in design reviews

  • Verifying relay settings, meter configurations, and controller programming delivered by third-party integrators against approved settings files and design documents

  • Owning site readiness on assigned projects by validating installation quality and accuracy of balance-of-plant systems such as fuel, electrical, metering, protection relays, and communications; developing punch lists and driving issues to closure when discrepancies are found

  • Validating electrical and mechanical installations against drawings and specifications by witnessing and/or reviewing results of checks such as wiring and termination verification, grounding, insulation resistance and continuity testing, phase rotation, and electrical acceptance test (NETA) reports; and equipment setting and anchoring, gas piping pressure and leak tests, purging, ventilation and exhaust, and fuel regulator setup

  • Configuring equipment and verifying functional readiness of site-level control and communication systems prior to energization, including troubleshooting industrial communication networks (e.g., Modbus TCP/IP, EtherNet/IP, Profibus, OPC-UA)

  • Supporting integration with customer PLC/SCADA/HMI platforms (e.g., Ignition, SEL RTAC, Siemens WinCC, AVEVA Wonderware, Rockwell FactoryTalk, Schneider EcoStruxure) for system monitoring and control

  • Coordinating handoff to the generator commissioning team, confirming all site-level prerequisites are complete before units are started, and keeping project stakeholders updated on readiness status and next steps

  • Planning Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) and system-level validation, defining acceptance criteria for customer and utility witness testing, and confirming that as-built operation matches design intent

  • Supporting Permission to Operate (PTO) by compiling documentation based on utility requirements and building an accurate submission package for the Interconnection team to issue to the utility

  • Owning site QA/QC documentation and ensuring systems are fully validated and ready for turnover to operations and the customer

  • Establishing repeatable processes, including ready-for-commissioning and ready-for-testing checklists, lookahead dashboards, SAT templates, equipment configuration and how-to guides, site procedures, etc

  • Travelling to project sites as needed to confirm readiness and perform necessary testing

Job Qualifications and Experience

  • B.S. degree in Electrical, Controls, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline. Equivalent field experience may be substituted

  • 5+ years in pre-commissioning, site commissioning, field applications, or controls engineering on power generation, battery storage, solar, microgrid, or industrial facility projects

  • Experience configuring, integrating, and troubleshooting devices and platforms such as:

  • Protective relays and automation controllers: SEL (relays, RTAC), GE Multilin, Beckwith, or ABB.

  • Revenue and power quality meters: SEL-735, Schneider ION, GE kV2c, or Itron

  • PLCs: Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix, Siemens S7, or Schneider Modicon

  • SCADA/HMI: Ignition, Siemens WinCC, AVEVA (Wonderware), or Rockwell FactoryTalk View

  • Working knowledge of industrial communication protocols (Modbus TCP/IP, EtherNet/IP, Profibus, OPC-UA, DNP3) and OT networking

  • Ability to interpret single-line and three-line diagrams, P&IDs, control narratives, and sequences of operation

  • Understanding of balance-of-plant systems, including fuel/gas, low- and medium-voltage electrical, metering, protection, and communications, with the ability to read construction plan sets and acceptance test reports and a working knowledge of NEC and NFPA 37/54

  • Experience planning and documenting Site Acceptance Testing and supporting utility witness testing for PTO

  • Familiarity with field safety practices and energization standards and procedures (e.g., NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout), including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures and arc flash hazard awareness

  • Strong analytical problem-solving skills with the ability to safely use standard electrical test equipment (multimeters, phase rotation meter, network cable/fiber tester, power quality analyzers) in an active construction or live-plant environment

  • Strong documentation and communication skills, and comfortable coordinating contractors, integrators, and customers on site

  • Self-directed, with an ownership mindset and enthusiasm for building repeatable processes within a growing team

Department Overview

The Office of Proposal & Award Management (OPAM), a unit within Research Development & Administration (RDA), supports OHSU's missions of healing, teaching and discovery by partnering with the research community to electively navigate the pre-award and post-­award administration on of sponsored projects. We support the OHSU research community with grant and contract proposal submission, contract negotiation, interpretation on and implementation on of sponsor terms and conditions and fiscal management of all sponsored projects.

Function/Duties of Position

The Sr. Industry Research Agreements Administrator is responsible for independently managing, analyzing, drafting, negotiating and executing complex sponsored project agreements funded by industry partners. Sr. Industry Research Agreements Administrator identifies and mitigates legal and business risks in agreements, ensures compliance with institutional policies, laws and regulations. This position must provide creative solutions to balance compliance and the needs of the research project.

Contract Management

  • Independently manage, analyze, draft, negotiate and execute complex sponsored project agreements funded by industry partners including, but not limited to, clinical trial agreements, collaboration agreements, investigator-initiated agreements, sponsored research agreements, master agreements, and business associate agreements.
  • Negotiate contract terms, incorporate appropriate terms, and as necessary, draft terms, working with various contracting parties to ensure that the requirements of the University and the industry sponsor are met while mitigating risk, maintaining the integrity of the research plan and protecting the intellectual property rights of the principal investigator and the University.
  • Consult and collaborate with CRSO, Collaborations and Entrepreneurship, OHSU Legal, Risk Management, ORIO, the funder, the sponsor and its affiliates, the principal investigator and his/her department where appropriate.
  • Ensure that contract payment schedules, budgets, reporting requirements, termination schedules, and deliverable schedules are complete, compatible with OHSU policy, practicable, and in the best interest of the principal investigator and OHSU.
  • Use extensive knowledge of applicable OHSU policy, public laws, regulations, and guidelines to translate program requirements into contract terms.
  • Verify necessary internal prior approvals, compliance requirements and documentation of subcontract institutions.

Customer Service

  • Provide superior customer service to internal and external contacts.
  • Clearly and reliably communicate with sponsors on behalf of OHSU (sponsors both internal and external to OHSU).
  • Provide subject matter expertise to entire Institution (including departments, hospital, foundation, and other contracting groups).
  • Develop and maintain working partnership with IRB, CRSO, and other internal offices as needed.
  • Actively participate as a team member by assisting others and freely sharing information.

Training

  • Provide leadership and training on internal processes and procedures to departmental staff and stakeholders, including training of Contract Administrators and Contract Coordinators.

  • Draft or modify policies, guidance, strategies, and practices to ensure researchers comply with contractual obligations under the contracts, including compliance with applicable state and federal regulation in conjunction with OHSU policies.

  • Develop contractual language, standard terms and clauses, templates and master agreements for training and use by the Industry Agreement team.

  • Participate in and contribute to externally focused departmental initiatives, such as contracts formal and informal training for department staff or faculty, brown-bag training sessions, and Research Administration Information Network (RAIN) meetings.

Skills and Abilities

  • Demonstrated excellent analytical skills with the ability to understand and synthesize complex guidelines and regulatory requirements.

jobs.excerpt: About MenloMenlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it.
jobs.description:
About Menlo

Menlo Research is an Applied R&D lab building Asimov, an open-source humanoid robot platform, and the full software stack that powers it. Our mission is to make humanoid labor economically viable, turning software into physical labor at scale. We build across the full stack: hardware architecture, locomotion, autonomy, simulation, and infrastructure. We move fast, ship to real robots, and open-source everything we can. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

The Role

Industrial design at Menlo is not cosmetic. Asimov is a physical product that will be assembled, operated, serviced, and iterated on, and how it looks, feels, and reads to the people around it is as consequential as how it performs. As our Industrial Designer, you will own the form language and physical identity of Asimov, from enclosures and surface treatments to ergonomics, CMF (color, material, finish), and packaging. You will translate that vision into parts that manufacture, assemble, and survive the real world, working shoulder to shoulder with mechanical and electrical engineers so every design decision holds up in production. This is design that ships to real hardware, not renders.

What You'll Do

  • Own industrial design for Asimov and the Menlo hardware family: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF, from concept and form language to production-ready enclosures, covers, and structural aesthetics

  • Turn mechanical and electrical constraints into clean, intentional design that does not hide the engineering

  • Prototype fast in foam, print, and machined parts, then iterate on real robots to test design intent

  • Own the CMF specification process: material selection, surface finish standards, color systems, and supplier engagement, and make sure those choices hold up in the field

  • Own design for manufacturing and assembly alongside mechanical engineering: DFM reviews, tolerance stack-ups, fastening, serviceability, part count, and assembly sequencing, catching issues before tooling

  • Design the human-facing details: grips, handles, access panels, indicators, and anything a person touches or reads

  • Shape the packaging and unboxing experience and user-facing documentation for Asimov kits and development hardware

  • Maintain design consistency across the Menlo hardware product family as the portfolio expands

What We Look For

  • A strong portfolio of shipped physical products, ideally complex electromechanical hardware, showing a consistent design sensibility under real technical constraints

  • 4 or more years shipping physical products: consumer electronics, robotics, medical devices, or similarly complex hardware

  • Deep industrial design fundamentals: form, proportion, ergonomics, and CMF

  • Strong proficiency in 3D modeling and surfacing (Alias, Rhino, SolidWorks, or equivalent) and rendering (KeyShot or similar), plus real DFM and DFA experience

  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes: injection molding, sheet metal, die casting, and surface finishing

  • Experience working directly with mechanical engineers and contract manufacturers in a fast, iterative environment

  • Comfort moving from sketch to prototype to production without needing a large team around you

  • Experience designing for humanoid or legged robots, cobots, or other electromechanical systems

  • A bias for building, testing on hardware, and iterating quickly, with the judgment to know when to obsess over a detail and when to ship

Nice to Have

  • Experience taking a product from zero to first production run

  • Hands-on shop skills: 3D printing, machining, moldmaking, and finishing

  • Exposure to DFM/DFA review in a high-mix, low-volume manufacturing context

  • Familiarity with simulation-driven or CAD-driven design workflows

  • A feel for how design and brand reinforce each other

  • Interest in open-source hardware communities

Why Join Menlo

You will define what a humanoid robot looks like at the moment the category is being written. That is a rare brief at this stage of a company, and it comes with the autonomy to match. Your work ships to real machines, in the real world, fast, alongside a small team that moves fast and takes the craft seriously. If you want your design to live in hardware people actually use rather than a slide, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you're excited about a role but don't meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. Menlo Research is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any legally protected characteristic. jobs.excerpt: Job Summary: Job Description: ABOUT MODAXOModaxo is a global collective of technology companies focused on People Transportation.
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Job Description:

ABOUT MODAXO

Modaxo is a global collective of technology companies focused on People Transportation. Our businesses deliver software and solutions that connect people with the places they need to go. We combine the community and accountability of local businesses with the reach, investment and shared learning of a global organisation.

We operate through a decentralised, multi-brand model. Our businesses retain local ownership and autonomy, while benefiting from relevant knowledge, proven practices and connections across the wider organisation. As Modaxo grows organically and through acquisition, our ability to capture, govern and reuse knowledge becomes increasingly important.


About the role

This is a new, high-visibility role with enterprise scope. It is designed to turn expertise spread across Modaxo businesses, functions and leaders into a trusted, accessible and reusable body of knowledge and learning content. This is a strategic knowledge and capability role, accountable for translating priority knowledge into practical application. You will set the knowledge and content strategy, establish the governance model, build a prioritised roadmap and source and curate content with subject matter experts. You will be accountable for the quality and coherence of the global layer, while business units remain free to create local content within agreed standards.

The role will succeed through judgement, influence and value creation. It must balance enterprise priorities with the realities of independently run businesses and make deliberate choices about what should be captured, standardised, scaled, signposted or managed within the businesses.


The role is remote and can be based in Eastern Canada or UK/Europe.


You will deliver

1. Enterprise Knowledge Strategy and Roadmap

  • Set the strategy. Define the enterprise knowledge and content strategy, aligned to Modaxo priorities and translated into a practical multi-year roadmap.
  • Prioritise for impact. Build a transparent intake and prioritisation approach with leaders and stakeholders, focusing effort on the knowledge that will create the greatest business value.
  • Own the global layer. Clarify which knowledge should be owned globally, which should remain local, and where common standards or signposting are sufficient.
  • Connect the portfolio. Create a coherent view across leadership content, functional playbooks, case studies, templates, AI capability content, acquisition learning and other reusable assets (understanding messaging and different channels and formats).

2. Networks, Stakeholder Engagement and Knowledge Sourcing

  • Build a strong network. Create and support a network of business-unit contributors, content owners and subject matter experts who help surface needs and validate knowledge.
  • Enable communities of practice. Partner with functional and business leaders to connect practitioners around shared challenges, proven approaches and emerging practice.
  • Make expertise visible. Develop simple ways for employees to identify where relevant expertise sits and how to access it.
  • Use live exchange selectively. Combine curated content with peer learning, case discussions, expert sessions and communities where human exchange adds more value than a static asset.

3. Knowledge Capture and Curation

  • Build a repeatable sourcing model. Build effective relationships and effective ways to source and identify potential stories.Create practical ways to extract expertise, lessons learned, playbooks and examples across Modaxo without placing unnecessary burden on business leaders and domain experts.
  • Capture what works. Identify proven practices and relevant stories, validate them with the right experts and turn them into reusable enterprise assets.
  • Protect critical expertise. Identify institutional knowledge at risk through leadership changes, retirement, transformation or acquisition, and establish proportionate methods to capture and transfer it.
  • Curate before creating. Reuse, adapt or signpost strong existing material where possible and commission new content only where a genuine gap exists.
  • Support acquisition learning. Build mechanisms to capture valuable expertise and practices from acquired businesses and make relevant Modaxo knowledge easier for new businesses and leaders to access.

4. Priority Capability and Learning Content

  • Lead the content roadmap. Translate Modaxo global priorities into a sequenced roadmap of flagship knowledge and learning content, with clear audiences, outcomes, owners and delivery routes for both business and functions.
  • Accelerate AI capability in the near term. Own the knowledge and learning content that helps leaders and employees understand the impact of AI, build relevant judgement and adapt their work, partnering with the AI CoE and Transformation team and other experts.
  • Build for application. Shape content around real decisions, tools, examples and behaviour change.
  • Commission specialist expertise. Pull from subject matter experts, other writers, facilitators and internal production teams as required. This role is accountable for the content outcome, not expected to be the technical expert on every topic.
  • Shape pathways and experiences. Connect assets into practical journeys for priority audiences, including leaders, new joiners, acquired businesses and functional communities.

6. Insight, Adoption and Continuous Improvement

  • Measure usefulness. Define measures that show whether people can find, trust, apply and reuse priority knowledge. Quality is more important than volume.
  • Build feedback loops. Use platform data, search patterns, stakeholder feedback and learner evidence to understand demand, gaps and friction.
  • Maintain a living backlog. Regularly review the roadmap based on strategic need, evidence of use, duplication and changing business priorities.
  • Demonstrate value. Report clearly on adoption, quality, reach, application and selected business outcomes.

7. Knowledge Architecture and Governance

  • Design the architecture. Establish a practical taxonomy, metadata and content model so people can find relevant knowledge by topic, role, business need, audience and format.
  • Set the quality bar. Define minimum standards for accuracy, format, accessibility, ownership, approval, source attribution and review.
  • Manage the lifecycle. Put clear review, version control, archive and retirement processes in place so the knowledge base remains current rather than becoming a static repository.
  • Create accountable ownership. Ensure priority assets have named business owners and subject matter validators, with clear responsibilities for maintenance.
  • Enable trusted search and reuse. Work with system and digital workplace specialists so content is structured, tagged and maintained in a way that supports effective discovery and appropriate future AI-assisted retrieval.

The role will work across the organisation and will need to build credibility with senior leaders and practitioners globally.

What success will look like?

First 12 months

  • A clear Modaxo global knowledge and content strategy, operating model and 12 & 24 month knowledge roadmap agreed with the relevant leaders and reviewed on a defined cadence.
  • Two to three flagship priorities delivered with evidence of improved understanding, application or time-to-competency. AI capability is an early priority. Evidence of building strong relationships with key stakeholders and identifying and delivering strong learning pathways and stories.
  • A functioning knowledge-sourcing network across businesses and functions, with a repeatable route for capturing stories, playbooks, tools and lessons learned.
  • A baseline view of current content, duplication, gaps and critical knowledge at risk, with agreed action for the highest-value areas.
  • Useful adoption and quality measures in place, moving beyond course completion to include findability, reuse, freshness, confidence and application.
  • A minimum viable enterprise governance framework in use, including named ownership, review cycles and retirement standards for priority content.
  • Clear working boundaries and productive partnerships with AI Transformation, HR Systems, Communications, IT and business-owned content experts.

Medium to long term

  • Modaxo has a trusted enterprise knowledge content and governance model that scales as the Group grows.
  • Priority expertise can be found and reused across businesses without undermining local autonomy.
  • Critical knowledge is captured and transferred during acquisition, leadership transition and organisational change.
  • Leaders and employees can access practical, current content that strengthens AI capability, leadership depth, succession and business performance.
  • Duplication is reduced and strong local practice is more consistently surfaced, validated and scaled.
  • Knowledge governance is embedded through a federated network of accountable owners and contributors.

About you

Experience and expertise

  • You will have a strong track record of setting enterprise knowledge, content or capability strategy and translating it into a focused, prioritised roadmap aligned with business needs.
  • You will demonstrated success influencing senior stakeholders and engaging business units across a complex, global, multi-entity decentralised organisation, including working effectively without formal authority and have proven ability to identify, source and draw out expertise, insight and effective practice from senior leaders, subject-matter experts and practitioners.
  • You have strong content strategy and editorial experience, with the ability to turn complex or specialist knowledge into clear, engaging and practical content without losing accuracy.
  • Experience selecting and combining different channels and formats to build practical capability. This may include messaging, playbooks, tools, case studies, digital resources, structured learning, live experiences and peer exchange, rather than written content alone.
  • You will be setting priorities, governance and quality standards, and commissioning work through subject-matter experts, writers, learning specialists, creative teams or external partners rather than personally producing every element, your track record of designing or materially improving an enterprise knowledge ecosystem, including practical approaches to sourcing, curation, ownership, findability, reuse and lifecycle management is key.
  • Experience using evidence, stakeholder feedback and analytics to prioritise a portfolio of knowledge and capability needs and to assess findability, adoption, application and value.
  • Good grounding in adult learning and instructional design, with experience shaping learning pathways and designing for retention, application and behaviour change rather than information delivery alone and well as shaping practical digital learning and capability solutions. Familiarity with authoring tools and platforms such as Articulate 360, Docebo, SharePoint or equivalent would be useful, but this is not a systems administration role.
  • Experience in a technology, software, professional services, acquisitive or federated business environment is strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting AI capability, acquisition integration, leadership development, organisational change or communities of practice would be valuable

Skills and attributes

  • Influential without authority: Builds trust across autonomous businesses and aligns diverse senior stakeholders around shared priorities, common standards, and practical outcomes.
  • Strategic and commercially grounded: Connects knowledge, capability, and content decisions to business priorities, focusing resources on areas of greatest value and impact.
  • Exceptional judgement: Distinguishes reusable organisational knowledge from information that should remain local or temporary, making sound decisions on what to create, curate, scale, adapt, or signpost.
  • Stakeholder management and executive influence: Extensive experience engaging, influencing, and building credibility with senior executives and business leaders in complex, matrixed organisations.
  • Knowledge architecture, storytelling, and content development: Strong ability to identify valuable insights within complex or technical information and transform them into compelling, accurate, and practical content for different audiences and channels.
  • Content governance and quality standards: Able to establish and maintain standards for accuracy, accessibility, consistency, localisation, and usability across a global content ecosystem.
  • Excellent communication and facilitation skills: Clear, concise written and verbal communicator in English, capable of tailoring messages, presentations, and workshops for executive, technical, and business audiences. Additional languages such as German, French, or Brazilian Portuguese are advantageous.
  • Builder mindset: Comfortable creating a new function, operating model, governance mechanisms, relationships, and ways of working in an evolving environment with limited infrastructure.
  • Data-informed decision maker: Uses quantitative and qualitative evidence to prioritise needs, improve adoption and content effectiveness, and measure business impact.
  • Curious but pragmatic about AI: Understands the implications of AI for knowledge management, content strategy, and organisational capability development while recognising where technical ownership resides.

Other

· UK/Europe or Eastern Canada, remote, with flexibility to work across time zones.

· International travel will be required periodically, anticipated at approximately two to four trips per year, subject to business need.

· Compensation will be competitive and aligned to experience and employing country.

Overview

Lumicera Health Services is seeking a Sr. Manager, Industry Relations to join our team!

The Sr. Manager, Industry Relations leads the team responsible for establishing, maintaining, and enhancing effective relationships with pharmaceutical manufacturers that produce specialty pharmaceuticals, and directs the negotiation of distribution and procurement contracts to ensure the specialty pharmacy can obtain specialty pharmaceuticals and pricing that meet the demands of its payers and patients. The Sr. Manager will lead and develop the Trade Relations team and Proposal Analysts and support Lumicera and its strategic partners in achieving business objectives and sourcing products competitively. This leader will interface with business leaders, pharmacists, legal, compliance, and external vendors with respect to specialty pharmacy services and trade duties.

Is this you? Find out more below!

  • Maintain relationships with pharmaceutical manufacturers and identify manufacturer program opportunities that support the specialty pharmacy’s strategic objectives.
  • Expand and negotiate manufacturer programs, including data and enhanced services programs.
  • Negotiate purchase discounts, including prompt pay, volume, and direct purchase discounts when appropriate, to maximize cost savings for the specialty pharmacy.
  • Manage enhanced services and data programs with manufacturers, including preparing and reporting on program performance and metrics during scheduled business reviews.
  • Develop and implement strategies and action plans for establishing and enhancing a competitive pharma contract structure that meets the current and future needs of the specialty pharmacy, Navitus PBM, payers, and patients/members, including appropriate agreements, analytical processes, and audit programs.
  • Oversee relations with data aggregators and manufacturer hub services, coordinating activities between Lumicera and those partners.
  • Assist with the co-development of annual budgets and monthly forecasts related to the procurement of specialty pharmaceutical products.
  • Represent the specialty pharmacy at leadership, industry, and trade groups.

  • Provide periodic reporting to leadership regarding activities, opportunities, performance, and emerging trends.
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Other duties as assigned.

  • Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy or PharmD degree required. Master of Business Administration (MBA) or other graduate degree preferred.

Job title: Area Business Manager - Allergy - Baltimore, MD

About the Job

Primary cities include: Baltimore MD, Columbia MD


Sanofi focuses on developing specialty treatments for debilitating diseases that are often difficult to diagnose and treat, providing hope to patients and their families.


Sanofi has pioneered the development and delivery of transformative therapies for patients affected by rare and debilitating diseases for over 30 years. We accomplish our goals through world-class research, collaboration with the global patient community, and with the compassion and commitment of our employees. With a focus on rare diseases, oncology, immunology and multiple sclerosis, we are dedicated to making a positive impact on the lives of the patients and families we serve. Sanofi’s portfolio of transformative therapies, which are marketed in countries around the world, represent groundbreaking and life-saving advances in medicine.


At Sanofi, we are committed to the growth of our people, connected in purpose by career, life and health.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you’ll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

At Sword, we’re building AI to heal billions and unlock humanity’s full potential. In doing so, we’re pioneering AI Care, a fundamentally new approach to healthcare built for medical reasoning, safety, and real-time treatment, not generic technology applied after the fact. As both a clinical-centric frontier AI lab and an applied AI platform, Sword is reimagining how care is delivered at scale, removing traditional barriers like appointments, waiting rooms, and stigma so more people can access the care they need—and ultimately get back to lives lived in full.

Since 2020, Sword has expanded across physical therapy, women’s health, cardiometabolic, and mental health, and is now moving beyond the session to a fully AI-native, 24/7 care program that brings physical activity, therapeutic exercise, psychotherapy, nutrition, and behavior change into one connected experience. More than 700,000 members across three continents have completed over 10 million AI sessions, helping 1,000+ enterprise clients avoid more than $1 billion in unnecessary healthcare costs. Backed by 42 clinical studies, 44+ patents, and more than $500 million raised from leading investors including Khosla Ventures, General Catalyst, and Founders Fund, Sword is defining a new standard for healthcare.

AI Proficiency at Sword

AI fluency is a core expectation at Sword. Every candidate is assessed against our three-level framework — be ready to share real examples of how AI is already part of how you work.

  • Explorer (Level 1) — Uses AI daily to boost personal productivity

  • Builder (Level 2) — Creates workflows and tools that elevate the whole team

  • Integrator (Level 3) — Embeds AI into products and processes at scale

Every hire must demonstrate at least Level 1. The expected level will vary depending on the seniority of the role.

Role

We are seeking a 10xer to lead our growth product efforts for maximizing our member acquisition and enrollment funnels. The ideal candidate is a high-velocity and analytical systems thinker who has deep expertise with building high performing conversion funnels. This is a role for a strategic thinker and a doer: someone who can see the big picture but isn't afraid to get their hands dirty building and executing.

This is a hands-on role. You'll manage two PMs and still write specs, analyze data, and ship experiments yourself. If you only want to be a people manager and want to operate through others, this isn't it.

This isn't a "maintenance" role; you will be the primary person accountable for step level improving all of our efforts on member growth through the funnel. You will own the entire funnel from landing pages through enrollment finished for our members. You are accountable for maximizing member acquisition and enrollment conversion.

Team

The Growth team is responsible for maximizing member growth across all solutions within Sword.

What you'll be doing:

  • The full member funnel. Landing pages, eligibility checks, registration, enrollment. You own the systems and the conversion metric through member enrollment.
  • The experimentation system, roadmap and decisions to drive results. You decide what we test, in what order, and what we do with the result.
  • Build systems that increase operational leverage. Client-specific requests, maintenance, new launches and new initiatives consume team capacity. You'll find what's repeatable, productize it into configuration instead of custom work, and use AI to automate the rest.

What you need to have:

  • 10+ years in product management building consumer-facing products or B2B2C platforms, including 4+ years managing PMs and Senior PMs.
  • Strong consumer product mindset with proven CRO track record. Deep understanding of consumer behavior, friction, and motivation, with experience building intuitive journeys
  • Deep expertise from acquisition through activation — landing page experimentation through to activated members, not just top-of-funnel. Come ready to walk through funnels you owned, the tests you ran, and the conversion rates before and after.
  • Ownership at scale. You've driven significant decisions and can engage deeply on data, experimentation, and technical tradeoffs. You work well with engineers because you understand what you're asking for.
